Chapter 1: Data Science as an Evidence and Decision Discipline

At 08:10 Monday, the identity team reports that confirmed account takeovers have nearly doubled: 145 last month versus 80 before. Login volume is flat. Fraud losses are up. The CISO asks, “Why, and what should we do today?”

That sentence hides different scientific jobs. Counting cases is descriptive. Locating the increase in recovery flows or customer cohorts is diagnostic. Estimating which current sessions will become takeovers is predictive. Estimating whether a new challenge would prevent compromise is causal. Allocating limited challenge capacity is prescriptive. Treating these jobs as interchangeable creates confident but invalid security programs.

This chapter follows the ATO problem from alarm to decision. Its structure is a sequence of increasingly demanding questions, each with its own estimand, evidence, and failure conditions.

The Monday-Morning Claim

An account takeover (ATO) occurs here when an unauthorized actor controls a customer account and the case is confirmed by a defined adjudication process. An alert is evidence, not the outcome.

Let (Y_i=1) when active account (i) has a confirmed takeover whose compromise date falls in month (t). The descriptive rate is

\[ R_t=\frac{\sum_{i\in A_t}Y_i}{|A_t|}, \]

where (A_t) is the population at risk. A numerator alone can manufacture a crisis when the customer base grows. A rate alone can hide a large workload. Report both, with label maturity.

Confirmed cases are delayed observations. If cases take nine days to adjudicate, comparing incomplete August labels with mature July labels biases the trend. A new customer-notification campaign may increase confirmations without changing compromise. The first task is a measurement audit: did compromise, observation, or adjudication change?

Population, unit, and clock

  • Population: consumer accounts eligible to authenticate, excluding tests, employees, and already locked accounts.
  • Unit: account-day for exposure, login session for challenge decisions, or account-month for reporting.
  • Clock: login, compromise, report, and adjudication times are distinct.

A row is an observation. A feature is available evidence, such as distinct networks used in the prior week. A label is the recorded training signal, such as an adjudicator disposition. A target is what a model estimates. An outcome is what happens in the world. Labels are fallible measurements of outcomes.

Five Questions Hidden in One Incident

What changed? Descriptive work

The descriptive estimand is the change in mature incidence:

\[ \Delta_R=R_{\text{current}}-R_{\text{baseline}}. \]

It says nothing about cause. Compute it by acquisition channel, account age, authentication method, recovery path, and telemetry coverage. Denominators must follow each segment. “Forty cases used recovery” is meaningless without the number of recovery attempts.

Description also audits data quality. A rise isolated to one adjudication queue may be workflow. A rise paired with lower sensor coverage may understate harm. This stage earns the right to ask harder questions.

Where is the mechanism? Diagnostic work

Diagnosis searches for explanations consistent with evidence. Excess cases after email changes and password resets suggest a recovery mechanism but do not prove that recovery caused the increase.

Compare compromised accounts with eligible accounts from the same period. Investigate releases, controls, marketing, bot traffic, and staffing. A field populated after support opens a case is a consequence of detection, not a precursor.

The output is a ranked hypothesis set with disconfirming checks: credential stuffing rose from residential proxies; a release weakened device binding; support improved confirmation; or one partner cohort was compromised. Each predicts a different observable pattern.

Which sessions will become takeovers? Predictive work

For decision-time evidence (X=x), the estimand is

\[ p(x)=P(Y^{14d}=1\mid X=x), \]

where (Y^{14d}) means confirmed ATO within fourteen days. A model may rank well without explaining cause. Device novelty can predict ATO even if forcing known devices would be harmful.

Prediction needs deployment-shaped data: features reconstructed at login time, outcomes matured for fourteen days, and temporal validation. Random row splits leak recurring accounts and campaigns. Accuracy is useless at rare base rates; calibration, precision at capacity, recall, and workload matter.

Would intervention prevent harm? Causal work

Let treatment (A) be a phishing-resistant step-up. For eligible sessions, define potential outcomes (Y_i(1)) with challenge and (Y_i(0)) without it. The causal estimand is

\[ \tau_E=E[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid E=1]. \]

Only one potential outcome is observed. Naively comparing challenged and unchallenged sessions is biased because current policy challenges riskier traffic. Identification needs randomization, a credible natural experiment, or explicit assumptions with sensitivity analysis. A phased randomized rollout can estimate intention to treat while retaining emergency overrides. A predictive score is not a treatment-effect estimate.

What should the system do? Prescriptive work

Prescription chooses actions under constraints. It uses descriptive facts, predicted risk, causal effects, friction, and capacity. A policy may reserve passkey challenges for sessions with high compromise risk and contexts where challenge is effective.

Constraints belong in the specification: at most 6,000 daily challenges; no SMS fallback for administrators; abandonment increase below 0.3 percentage points; human review for high-value transfers. The answer is a policy frontier, not an unexplained threshold. If challenge does not help stolen active sessions, higher predictive precision does not solve that decision.

The Estimand Ledger

ProductUnit/populationEstimandEvidenceInvalid shortcut
Trendactive account-monthmature ATOs per 100,000denominators, mature casesraw counts
Diagnosiseligible account-dayexcess incidence by mechanismaligned telemetry, release historyalert mix equals attack mix
Rankinglogin session(P(Y^{14d}=1\mid X))as-of features, mature outcomesrandom split
Evaluationeligible session(E[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid E=1])randomized or credible assignmenttreated/untreated comparison
Policydaily sessionsprevented ATOs under capacityrisk, effects, cost, capacitymaximize AUC

Every artifact should name the row it supports. If it supports no decision and improves no other artifact’s validity, it may not deserve production ownership.

Lab: Turn the Alarm into Evidence

Save as ato_evidence.py and run with the book environment.

from collections import defaultdict

rows = [
    ("July", "password", 60_000, 48, True),
    ("July", "passkey", 40_000, 12, True),
    ("August", "password", 61_000, 105, True),
    ("August", "passkey", 42_000, 14, True),
    ("September", "password", 63_000, 82, False),
]

monthly = defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0])
for month, cohort, active, cases, mature in rows:
    if mature:
        monthly[month][0] += active
        monthly[month][1] += cases

for month in ("July", "August"):
    active, cases = monthly[month]
    print(f"{month}: {cases} cases; {cases / active * 100_000:.1f} per 100k")

j = monthly["July"]; a = monthly["August"]
print(f"absolute rate change: {(a[1]/a[0] - j[1]/j[0]) * 100_000:.1f} per 100k")

selected = {(m, c): (n, y) for m, c, n, y, mature in rows if mature}
for cohort in ("password", "passkey"):
    jn, jy = selected[("July", cohort)]; an, ay = selected[("August", cohort)]
    print(f"{cohort}: {(ay/an - jy/jn) * 100_000:+.1f} per 100k")

questions = {
    "descriptive": "How much did mature ATO incidence change?",
    "diagnostic": "Which cohort and mechanism explain the excess?",
    "predictive": "Which sessions will be confirmed within 14 days?",
    "causal": "Would a passkey challenge prevent takeover?",
    "prescriptive": "Which sessions consume limited challenge capacity?",
}
for kind, question in questions.items():
    print(f"{kind:12s} {question}")

Expected output:

July: 60 cases; 60.0 per 100k
August: 119 cases; 115.5 per 100k
absolute rate change: 55.5 per 100k
password: +92.1 per 100k
passkey: +3.3 per 100k
descriptive  How much did mature ATO incidence change?
diagnostic   Which cohort and mechanism explain the excess?
predictive   Which sessions will be confirmed within 14 days?
causal       Would a passkey challenge prevent takeover?
prescriptive Which sessions consume limited challenge capacity?

The fixture does not prove passwords caused the incident. It establishes concentration and excludes immature September. The next analysis must test mechanisms and population composition.

Building an Evidence Program

First frame the claim: population, unit, time origin, outcome, decision, and estimand. Next preserve event, ingestion, availability, intervention, and adjudication times. Audit sensor coverage, identity resolution, adjudication delay, and sampling. Reproduce the headline before modeling. Select the minimum adequate method: a rate table may resolve the initial alarm; logistic regression may rank sessions; randomization may be required for intervention effect.

Validation must resemble use. Recreate future traffic, label delay, capacity, and attack campaigns. Deployment versions the eligible population, features, model, treatment rules, and override behavior. Monitoring covers denominator shifts, maturity, treatment compliance, calibration, and adversarial displacement.

Reproducibility means another qualified person can reconstruct the result from versioned code, immutable inputs or snapshots, environment metadata, and a decision log. Peer review should challenge exclusions, temporal joins, outcomes, and identification assumptions, not merely style. Ethical review asks whether collection is proportionate and intervention friction is fairly distributed.

Simplicity reduces assumptions and review surface, but does not excuse weak design. No model repairs an undefined outcome. No causal method repairs severe interference without modeling it.

Case Resolution: What Can Be Said

Suppose the excess begins six hours after a release stopped invalidating old recovery tokens. It is concentrated in password accounts completing recovery. Rollback reduces suspicious completions immediately, while confirmed outcomes mature later.

The defensible report says the mature incidence increase is real; most excess cases use password recovery; timing and code inspection implicate stale tokens; emergency rollback is justified by mechanism evidence and reversibility; takeovers prevented are not yet identified; and a passkey experiment concerns future policy, not historical cause.

This is more useful than “the model found root cause.” It tells leaders what is observed, inferred, actionable, and unknown.

Analytical Ethics and Review Gates

An ATO program observes intimate behavior: devices, travel patterns, recovery attempts, network location, and sometimes financial activity. “Useful for prediction” is not sufficient authority to collect a field. The team should document purpose, retention, access, and whether a less intrusive signal can answer the same question. Raw IP histories need not be exposed to every model developer merely because a derived network-change feature is useful.

Intervention burden also deserves analysis. Step-up challenges can disproportionately affect travelers, accessibility-tool users, shared-device households, and customers in regions where preferred factors are unavailable. This is not resolved by deleting protected attributes. Without carefully governed cohort evaluation, the team may be unable to discover concentrated harm. Access to sensitive cohort attributes should be separated from routine scoring and used under an approved evaluation protocol.

Peer review should stop an analysis when the claimed population differs from the sampled population, label maturity is ignored, availability time cannot be reconstructed, or causal language exceeds the design. A reviewer should be able to answer four questions from the artifact alone: What quantity was estimated? Which observations could enter it? What assumptions connect data to the claim? What result would reverse the recommendation?

The incident tempo does not remove these gates. It changes the level of evidence appropriate to an action. A reversible rollback with strong mechanism evidence may proceed before a precise causal effect is available. A permanent program that challenges millions of customers requires stronger evaluation. Match evidentiary burden to action scale, reversibility, and potential harm.

Diagnostic Stop Rules

Investigations can become endless correlation hunts. Establish stop rules before opening another dashboard. Stop expanding diagnosis when a mechanism is reproduced technically, its predicted telemetry pattern appears, a reversible mitigation exists, and remaining uncertainty will not change the immediate action. Continue outcome measurement afterward to quantify effect.

Conversely, stop model development and return to instrumentation when confirmation coverage cannot be estimated, principal resolution is unstable, or key source timestamps reflect batch load rather than availability. A sophisticated classifier trained under those conditions converts measurement failure into numerical confidence.

Maintain a claim register with status values such as observed, supported mechanism, causally identified, contradicted, and open. Link each status to evidence and date it. During a fast-moving incident, this prevents yesterday’s working theory from becoming tomorrow’s unquestioned fact. It also creates a clean handoff from incident response to the longer-lived prevention program.

Evidence quality should be visible in the decision memo. A mature rate from a stable denominator may receive a high grade; a mechanism supported by logs and code reproduction a moderate-to-high grade; an extrapolated treatment effect from another population a low grade. Grades do not replace argument. They force the author to state why one claim is firmer than another. Record dissent as well: if identity engineering disputes timestamp semantics, the unresolved dispute belongs beside the recommendation. This habit makes later incident review scientific rather than ceremonial and prevents an executive slide from flattening heterogeneous evidence into one unjustified confidence label.

  • NIST, Digital Identity Guidelines: Authentication and Lifecycle Management, SP 800-63B. https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html

Interview Practicum

The Incident Changes Mid-Answer

Panel prompt

“Confirmed ATOs rose from 80 to 145. Design the response.” Five minutes later: “Support launched a self-service confirmation form halfway through.” Later still: “You may challenge only 5% of sessions, and fraud will not randomize obviously high-risk traffic.”

Clarifying branches

Ask when compromise occurs relative to confirmation; whether both counts are mature under one rule; how active accounts changed; which releases and controls moved; how challenge eligibility is defined; what “obviously high-risk” means; and whether boundary traffic can be randomized. The support form threatens comparability. Capacity turns ranking into allocation. Safety restrictions change the experiment’s target population.

Worked Answer

Strong answer

Reproduce the increase by compromise month with a fixed maturity window and active-account denominator. Model confirmations as the product of latent compromise and observation. Backfill historical cases to estimate how the new form changed reporting delay and confirmation probability; report bounds if cases cannot be recovered.

Diagnose concentration using recovery path, factor, account age, device continuity, network, segment, and telemetry health. Tie discontinuities to releases. Keep association language until intervention effects are identified.

Define prediction as confirmed ATO within fourteen days and validate temporally. At 5% capacity, report precision and captured cases at that operating point, calibration by cohort, and workload.

Estimate challenge effectiveness only where randomization is ethical. Route obvious-high-risk traffic to safety action; randomize eligible boundary sessions. The intention-to-treat estimate applies to that boundary population, not automatically to forced-action sessions. Measure completion, abandonment, fraud, and displacement into recovery.

Recommend emergency rollback when mechanism evidence and reversibility justify it, but label prevented cases as pending. Launch a bounded challenge experiment only after calibration and data-health checks.

Worked detail

If 80 observed cases had 0.70 confirmation probability and 145 had 0.90 after the form, simplified latent counts are (80/0.70=114.3) and (145/0.90=161.1). The observed 81% increase becomes an estimated 41% latent-count increase. This is sensitivity analysis, not truth; constant sensitivity is a strong assumption.

For assignment (Z), receipt (A), and outcome (Y), report (E[Y\mid Z=1]-E[Y\mid Z=0]) as intention to treat. Assignment can instrument receipt only if exclusion, relevance, and monotonicity are plausible.

Weak answers

  • “Train XGBoost on all logins” ignores the changed observation process.
  • “Block more because cases rose 81%” ignores denominators and maturity.
  • “Device novelty caused ATO” mistakes prediction for cause.
  • “A/B test everyone” ignores safety constraints.
  • “Never experiment in security” leaves ethical policy effects unknowable.

Follow-Up Questions and Answers

Follow-up probes with answers

Cases are selected by the current detector. What now? Adjudicate a probability sample outside its boundary and weight by sampling probabilities. Where withholding action is unsafe, give bounds rather than fictional recall.

Attackers adapt? Treat channel displacement as an outcome, time-index estimates, and refresh the threat model.

Passkey users differ from password users? Raw rate differences are not passkey effects. Require a credible counterfactual and state the overlap population.

When stop the experiment? Stop for predefined harm, data-integrity failure, abandonment, or overwhelming efficacy under a valid sequential design—not repeated ordinary (p)-value peeking.

Communication drills

Thirty seconds: “Separate compromise from changed confirmation, locate the mature denominator-correct excess, estimate fourteen-day session risk for the 5% capacity decision, and estimate challenge effect in an ethical boundary experiment. Keep emergency mitigation separate from claims about prevented cases.”

Five minutes: Lead with the four estimands: incidence change, concentration, session risk, and treatment effect. Explain observation correction, temporal validation, boundary randomization, capacity metrics, and what remains unidentified.

Key Takeaways

  • Description, diagnosis, prediction, causation, and prescription answer different questions.
  • Write population, unit, clock, outcome, and estimand before choosing a method.
  • Labels measure outcomes through an observation process that can change independently.
  • Prediction identifies neither historical cause nor intervention effect.
  • Capacity and safety are part of the scientific problem.
  • Distinguish what is observed, inferred, identified, and unknown.

Chapter 2: Data Types, Structures, and When to Use Them

A security lake receives four objects: an authentication event, an analyst paragraph, a NetFlow record, and an identity-entitlement edge. They all concern the same investigation, but forcing them into one wide table destroys meaning. This chapter treats representation as type design. We will build a catalog, inspect a mixed fixture, and show which operations are valid for each field.

A Type System for Security Evidence

A data type is a set of possible values plus valid operations. Storage syntax is secondary. An IPv4 address stored as an integer is not a quantity; adding two addresses is meaningless. A severity encoded 1–5 is ordered, but the distance from 1 to 2 need not equal the distance from 4 to 5. A timestamp is not a duration. These distinctions prevent silent analytical errors.

Numeric families

Counts are nonnegative integers: failed logins, packets, findings. Their variance often grows with the mean, and exposure differs, so rates may be more comparable. Continuous measurements include latency and bytes after aggregation. Ratio-scale values have a meaningful zero; ratios are meaningful. Interval-scale values have meaningful differences but an arbitrary zero, as with Celsius. Money is ratio-like within a currency and valuation time, but exchange and inflation complicate comparisons.

A rate needs numerator, denominator, and interval. failures_per_attempt differs from failures_per_minute. Store the components when possible; a precomputed rate hides low-denominator instability.

Categorical families

Nominal categories such as operating system have equality but no order. Ordinal categories such as low/medium/high have order but unknown spacing. Binary flags need explicit positive semantics. Multilabel observations may carry several ATT&CK techniques. High-cardinality categories—user IDs, device IDs, process hashes—are identifiers, not automatically model-ready categories.

Encoding nominal values as integers invents order. One-hot encoding can explode dimensions. Hashing trades collisions for bounded size. Learned embeddings can capture similarity but require enough data and careful unknown handling. The choice follows the task, not the source database type.

Time is several types

A UTC timestamp identifies an instant. A local calendar value depends on a timezone and daylight-saving rules. A duration measures elapsed time. A sequence preserves order. A time series associates measurements with regular or irregular times. An event stream adds arrival behavior: late, duplicated, and out-of-order messages.

Store RFC 3339 timestamps with offsets at boundaries and normalize instants to UTC internally. Preserve source timezone where local business behavior matters. Never infer elapsed time by subtracting naive local timestamps across a daylight-saving transition.

Text, code, and documents

Analyst notes are not merely long categories. They contain tokens, sentences, entities, assertions, negation, uncertainty, and sensitive data. Source code has syntax trees and control flow. Prompts have roles and message boundaries. Security reports have sections, citations, indicators, and provenance.

Representations include raw immutable text, normalized text for search, token or n-gram features, embeddings for retrieval, and structured extractions. Retain offsets from extracted facts back to source spans. An embedding is a lossy index, not evidence; investigators must recover the original passage.

Network and spatial values

IP addresses support prefix membership, version, and equality—not arithmetic distance as ordinary integers. Ports are bounded identifiers with conventions, not continuous quantities. Latitude and longitude require spherical distance and privacy controls. “Country” may describe IP geolocation, billing, residence, or legal entity; name the semantics and provider version.

NetFlow is a directional summary with source/destination addresses and ports, protocol, byte and packet counts, and interval. Reversing direction changes interpretation. NAT and proxies mean an address is not an identity.

Graphs

An identity graph contains typed nodes and edges: user member_of group, service principal has_role subscription, device managed_by tenant. Edges often have validity intervals and provenance. A static adjacency table loses the difference between current and historical permission.

Graph questions include reachability, shortest attack path, neighborhood aggregation, centrality, and community structure. Exporting degrees into a tabular model is useful but cannot answer arbitrary path queries. Graph storage is justified by traversal workload, not visual appeal.

Binary, packet, image, audio, and multimodal evidence

Executable bytes support hashes, sections, imports, entropy, and disassembly. Packet captures preserve payload and timing but raise storage and privacy costs. Screenshots may contain phishing cues and text. Audio may contain voice, timing, and codec artifacts. A multimodal record must preserve modality-specific preprocessing and synchronization; concatenating unrelated vectors does not create coherent evidence.

Shape: How Observations Relate

Cross-sectional data take one measurement per unit. Longitudinal data repeat units. Panel data organize multiple units across times. Cohort data align units by an origin such as enrollment. Survival data record time to outcome plus censoring. A user with no observed takeover by study end is right-censored, not proven permanently safe.

Structured data have explicit fields; semi-structured events have envelopes plus variable nested payloads; unstructured artifacts lack a uniform field model. “Unstructured” does not mean structure-free: documents and binaries have rich internal grammars.

Static snapshots answer state questions. Streams answer timely change questions but require watermarks, idempotency, and late-data policy. A snapshot of permissions cannot reconstruct which access existed at incident time unless validity history is retained.

Schema Catalog: One Investigation, Four Stores

Authentication event envelope

auth_event
  event_id: uuid                  identity, not a feature magnitude
  occurred_at: timestamp[UTC]     source-reported instant
  observed_at: timestamp[UTC]     collector availability
  principal_id: opaque_id         join key with tenant scope
  outcome: enum{success,failure,challenge}
  source_ip: ip_address
  factors: set<enum>
  latency_ms: duration
  raw: json                       immutable source payload

The envelope is append-only. Corrections become new records or versioned normalization outputs. observed_at makes point-in-time reconstruction possible.

Analyst document

case_note
  note_id: uuid
  case_id: opaque_id
  author_role: enum
  created_at: timestamp[UTC]
  body: sensitive_text
  assertions: list<{span, predicate, object, confidence}>
  embedding_model: nullable model_version
  embedding: nullable vector<float>

Access control applies to source text and derived vectors. Assertions preserve span provenance and distinguish “user denied travel” from “user traveled.”

Flow fact

network_flow
  sensor_id: opaque_id
  start_at/end_at: timestamp[UTC]
  src/dst_ip: ip_address
  src/dst_port: uint16
  protocol: enum
  packets/bytes: count
  sampling_rate: probability

Sampled counts require weighting. Zero packets is not the same as missing telemetry.

Temporal identity edge

identity_edge
  subject_id/object_id: scoped_id
  relation: enum
  valid_from: timestamp[UTC]
  valid_to: nullable timestamp[UTC]
  asserted_at: timestamp[UTC]
  source: system_version

valid_to IS NULL means currently open, not unknown forever. An as-of query requires valid_from <= t and (valid_to > t or null), plus asserted_at <= t if replay must respect availability.

Representation Decision Matrix

EvidenceCanonical storageUseful transformationSuitable analysisCommon category error
Failed-login countinteger plus exposurerate, log1p, rolling sumcount model, thresholdtreat 2 and 200 attempts equally
Severityordered enumordinal encodingrank tests, ordinal modelassume equal spacing
User IDscoped opaque stringjoins, frequency, hashingentity historynumeric scaling
Timestamptimezone-aware instanthour, recency, windowstemporal split, survivalparse as local naive time
IP addressnative IP/prefixsubnet, ASN, reputationprefix matching, graphEuclidean integer distance

Entitlementtemporal typed edgepaths, degreesreachability, GNNsnapshot as timeless truth
Malware bytesimmutable blobimports, sections, hashesstatic analysis, classifierdecode arbitrary bytes as text

Lab: Inspect and Type a Mixed Fixture

The lab uses only the standard library. It rejects seductive coercions and emits a compact dictionary.

from datetime import datetime
from ipaddress import ip_address
import json

records = [
    {"field": "attempts", "value": 12, "logical": "count"},
    {"field": "severity", "value": "high", "logical": "ordinal"},
    {"field": "principal_id", "value": "00731", "logical": "opaque_id"},
    {"field": "occurred_at", "value": "2026-08-20T13:45:00Z", "logical": "instant"},
    {"field": "source_ip", "value": "2001:db8::8", "logical": "ip_address"},
    {"field": "analyst_note", "value": "User denies this sign-in.", "logical": "sensitive_text"},
    {"field": "techniques", "value": ["T1078", "T1110"], "logical": "set[nominal]"},
]

def validate(row):
    value, kind = row["value"], row["logical"]
    if kind == "count":
        assert isinstance(value, int) and value >= 0
    elif kind == "ordinal":
        assert value in {"low", "medium", "high", "critical"}
    elif kind == "opaque_id":
        assert isinstance(value, str)
    elif kind == "instant":
        datetime.fromisoformat(value.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    elif kind == "ip_address":
        value = f"IPv{ip_address(value).version}"
    elif kind == "set[nominal]":
        assert len(value) == len(set(value))
        value = sorted(value)
    elif kind == "sensitive_text":
        value = f"{len(value.split())} tokens (redacted)"
    return {"field": row["field"], "logical_type": kind, "preview": value}

for item in records:
    print(json.dumps(validate(item), sort_keys=True))

Expected output:

{"field": "attempts", "logical_type": "count", "preview": 12}
{"field": "severity", "logical_type": "ordinal", "preview": "high"}
{"field": "principal_id", "logical_type": "opaque_id", "preview": "00731"}
{"field": "occurred_at", "logical_type": "instant", "preview": "2026-08-20T13:45:00Z"}
{"field": "source_ip", "logical_type": "ip_address", "preview": "IPv6"}
{"field": "analyst_note", "logical_type": "sensitive_text", "preview": "4 tokens (redacted)"}
{"field": "techniques", "logical_type": "set[nominal]", "preview": ["T1078", "T1110"]}

The leading zeros in principal_id survive because it is not a number. IPv6 is validated without logging the address. The multilabel set is canonicalized. The note preview avoids reproducing sensitive text.

Mixed-Data Representation Lab

One investigation can be rendered as table, sequence, document retrieval result, and graph neighborhood. Each view answers a different query.

from collections import Counter, defaultdict

auth = [
    ("u1", 1, "failure", "d1"),
    ("u1", 2, "success", "d2"),
    ("u2", 3, "success", "d3"),
]
notes = {"u1": "customer denies login from new device"}
edges = [("u1", "member_of", "admins"), ("admins", "can_access", "billing")]

print("tabular", dict(sorted(Counter(x[2] for x in auth).items())))
print("sequence", [x[2] for x in sorted(auth) if x[0] == "u1"])
query = {"denies", "device"}
hits = [uid for uid, text in notes.items() if query <= set(text.split())]
print("text_hits", hits)

graph = defaultdict(list)
for left, relation, right in edges:
    graph[left].append((relation, right))
frontier = ["u1"]
paths = []
for _ in range(2):
    node = frontier.pop(0)
    for relation, nxt in graph[node]:
        paths.append(f"{node}-{relation}->{nxt}")
        frontier.append(nxt)
print("graph", paths)

Expected output:

tabular {'failure': 1, 'success': 2}
sequence ['failure', 'success']
text_hits ['u1']
graph ['u1-member_of->admins', 'admins-can_access->billing']

The count view loses order; the sequence preserves it. Keyword retrieval finds a note but not its truth. The graph exposes transitive access. No single representation dominates.

Labels, Weak Labels, and Censoring

A confirmed incident label may be precise but selected: only alerted cases receive investigation. A user report is weak evidence with variable delay. A vendor verdict can change. A rule hit is a heuristic label, not ground truth. Keep label source, version, time, and confidence separate from the target.

Unobserved does not mean negative. In survival data, an account observed for seven days without ATO is censored at seven days. In positive-unlabeled learning, unlabeled examples contain negatives and undiscovered positives. In streaming systems, a late label may revise an earlier training snapshot. Schema catalogs should therefore describe outcome maturity and revision behavior.

Catalog Governance and Compatibility

A data dictionary becomes useful when it is executable. Each field entry should include logical type, null semantics, unit, allowed range or vocabulary, sensitivity classification, owner, source, event-time meaning, availability expectation, retention, and known revisions. Examples are valuable, but examples cannot replace constraints.

Schema compatibility has several dimensions. A change can be syntactically additive yet semantically breaking: keeping country as a string while changing it from billing country to IP-geolocation country will pass parsers and corrupt trends. Renaming an enum is obvious; changing the population represented by a boolean is not. Version meaning, not merely serialization.

Producers should publish contract tests. Consumers should test unknown enum values, absent optional fields, duplicates, delayed events, and mixed schema versions. Rejecting every new value creates outages; silently mapping every unknown to “other” can hide attacks and rollout defects. The contract must state whether unknown means unsupported, newly introduced, malformed, or intentionally withheld.

For privacy, classify derived data as carefully as raw data. Hashing an email does not make it anonymous when the hash is stable and linkable. Embeddings may retain sensitive semantic information. Graph neighborhoods can reveal privileged roles. Apply tenant scope, access control, deletion obligations, and retention to derivatives, indexes, caches, and training snapshots.

Choosing Physical Layout from Access Patterns

Logical modeling precedes physical layout. Columnar files suit scans over selected fields and compress repeated values. Row stores suit keyed transactional reads. Inverted indexes suit lexical retrieval. Vector indexes suit approximate semantic neighbors. Graph engines suit variable-depth traversal. Stream logs suit ordered append and replay. These are workload claims that should be benchmarked.

Partitioning by date accelerates bounded time scans but can create tiny files at low volume. Partitioning by high-cardinality user ID is usually disastrous. Clustering or sorting by tenant and time may improve pruning without creating a directory per identity. Storage statistics themselves can leak tenant size, so operational metadata also needs authorization.

Materialized representations need freshness contracts. An online feature may use a five-minute identity-neighborhood cache while an investigator queries the authoritative temporal graph. Both are correct for their declared use, but they are not interchangeable. Record build time, source watermark, and transformation version so disagreement can be explained.

Representation choices should be reversible where uncertainty is high. Preserve an immutable canonical artifact, then derive tables, indexes, vectors, and graph projections. Reversibility does not mean retaining everything forever; retention and deletion must be enforced at the canonical and derived layers. It means avoiding an irreversible lossy transform as the only surviving evidence.

Benchmark with representative queries before adopting another store. Measure ingest throughput, bounded-time scans, key lookup latency, traversal depth, retrieval recall, authorization overhead, backfill duration, and deletion propagation. Include failure experiments: one region unavailable, an index six hours stale, or a schema version arriving early. A fast happy-path benchmark says little about investigative reliability. Document the exit cost, including how canonical data can be exported without losing temporal semantics. Specialized infrastructure is justified when it produces a measured capability the existing platform cannot meet, not when its data model merely resembles a whiteboard drawing. Measure semantics first; optimize their physical execution second.

  • IETF RFC 8200, Internet Protocol, Version 6. https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8200
  • W3C, RDF 1.1 Concepts and Abstract Syntax. https://www.w3.org/TR/rdf11-concepts/

Interview Practicum

The Architecture Whiteboard

Prompt and constraint cards

“Represent authentication events, analyst notes, NetFlow, and an identity graph for detection and investigation.” Then the panel reveals: notes contain regulated data; flows are sampled 1:100; entitlement edges arrive up to six hours late; investigators need 90-day replay; and the feature service needs results in 100 ms.

Worked Answer

Strong answer

Use an immutable event envelope for authentication with occurrence and observation times. Store typed normalized columns beside raw versioned payloads. Partition by event date and tenant, but avoid putting sensitive identity values in paths. Use a protected document store and inverted/vector indexes for notes; retain source spans and apply the same access policy to embeddings.

Store flows in a columnar fact table with direction, interval, counters, and sampling rate. Weighted aggregate estimates may multiply counts by 100, but uncertainty and collector loss must be distinguished. Store temporal identity edges with validity and assertion intervals. Materialize bounded neighborhoods for the low-latency feature path while keeping a graph-capable historical store for replay.

Use scoped stable IDs and a governed identity-resolution table. Do not join on email text or IP. Every derived object records source versions and as-of time. The 100-ms service reads precomputed typed features; investigation queries can tolerate slower document and graph traversal. Replay blocks facts whose observation time exceeds the historical decision time.

Tradeoffs

A single warehouse simplifies governance and batch joins but may serve graph traversal and text retrieval poorly. Specialized stores improve workloads but multiply consistency and authorization surfaces. Choose the smallest set that meets measured workloads, and publish canonical semantics centrally. Parquet is efficient for scans, not point mutation. A graph database helps variable-depth traversal, not simple one-hop joins. Vector retrieval improves semantic recall but requires evaluation and source recovery.

Weak answers

  • “Put everything in JSON” avoids schema design and weakens constraints.
  • “Use a graph database for all data” confuses connectedness with every workload.
  • “Convert IDs and IPs to integers” invents numeric meaning and breaks formatting.
  • “Embed the notes and delete text” discards evidence and provenance.
  • “Missing edge means no access” ignores late arrival and sensor coverage.

Follow-Up Questions and Answers

Follow-up probes with answers

How do you version a schema without breaking consumers? Use additive evolution by default, stable field identifiers, compatibility tests, explicit semantic versions for changed meaning, and dual-read migration for breaking changes.

How do you represent a deleted entitlement? Close the edge validity interval; do not delete historical state required for replay. Record when the deletion assertion became available.

Can sampled NetFlow identify one connection? No. Sampling supports certain aggregate estimates; it does not reconstruct omitted individual flows. State the sampling mechanism before weighting.

How do you test embeddings containing sensitive notes? Apply document authorization before retrieval, test cross-tenant isolation and memorization risks, minimize retained text, and log access without exposing content.

Communication drills

Thirty seconds: “Keep four canonical forms: typed immutable events, protected documents with span provenance, directional sampled flow facts, and temporal identity edges. Join them through scoped IDs and as-of semantics; materialize only the low-latency features needed online.”

Five minutes: Walk through logical types, canonical stores, transformations, workload indexes, late data, replay, privacy, and why no universal table or database is appropriate.

Key Takeaways

  • Logical type determines valid operations; physical storage does not create semantics.
  • Preserve counts and exposures, instants and durations, validity and availability.
  • IDs, IPs, ports, ranks, and timestamps must not be coerced into false quantities.
  • Text embeddings, graph features, and aggregates are derived views, not substitutes for evidence.
  • Censoring, weak labels, sampling, and late arrival belong in the schema contract.
  • Mixed security investigations need interoperable representations, not one universal shape.

Chapter 3: Probability, Statistics, and Uncertainty

A malware detector advertises 99% sensitivity and 99% specificity. The SOC hears “99% accurate.” At a base rate of one malicious file per thousand, however, most alerts are false. Probability supplies the missing denominator; statistics tells us how uncertain our measurements are; simulation shows what the queue may look like tomorrow.

This chapter is organized as a quantitative case file. We derive the alert calculation, examine distributions behind security counts and delays, construct intervals, test a policy change, perform a Bayesian update, and simulate operational load.

Case File A: The Alert That Sounds Certain

Let (M) denote malicious and (+) a positive detector result. Suppose

\[ P(M)=0.001,\quad P(+\mid M)=0.99,\quad P(-\mid \neg M)=0.99. \]

The false-positive rate is (P(+\mid\neg M)=0.01). Bayes’ theorem gives

\[ P(M\mid +)=\frac{P(+\mid M)P(M)}{P(+\mid M)P(M)+P(+\mid\neg M)P(\neg M)}. \]

Substitution yields

\[ \frac{0.99(0.001)}{0.99(0.001)+0.01(0.999)} =\frac{0.00099}{0.01098}=0.09016. \]

So an alert has about 9.0% posterior probability of malware. In one million files, the expected confusion matrix is 990 true alerts, 10 missed malware files, 9,990 false alerts, and 989,010 true negatives. Analysts receive 10,980 alerts; roughly eleven out of twelve are false.

The detector is not broken. The verbal summary was. Sensitivity and specificity condition on truth; an analyst needs probability of truth conditioned on the alert. Base rates connect them.

Odds form and sequential evidence

Bayes is often clearer in odds. Prior odds are

\[ O(M)=\frac{0.001}{0.999}=0.001001. \]

The positive likelihood ratio is (LR^+=0.99/0.01=99). Posterior odds equal prior odds times likelihood ratio:

\[ O(M\mid +)=0.001001\times99=0.099099. \]

Converting odds to probability gives (0.099099/(1+0.099099)=0.09016).

If an independent sandbox result has (LR^+=20), posterior odds become (1.98198), or probability (1.98198/2.98198=0.6647). Independence is a substantive assumption. Two engines trained on the same corpus and signatures may provide correlated evidence; multiplying their likelihood ratios overstates certainty.

Random Variables Behind Security Telemetry

A random variable maps uncertain outcomes to values. For Bernoulli (X\in\{0,1\}) with success probability (p),

\[ E[X]=p,\qquad Var(X)=p(1-p). \]

The sum of (n) independent Bernoulli trials is binomial:

\[ P(K=k)=\binom{n}{k}p^k(1-p)^{n-k}, \quad E[K]=np,\quad Var(K)=np(1-p). \]

It can model malicious files in a fixed batch when trials are sufficiently similar and independent. Campaign bursts violate those assumptions and inflate variance.

Poisson counts and exposure

For events arriving independently at constant rate (lambda),

\[ P(K=k)=e^{-\lambda}\frac{\lambda^k}{k!}, \quad E[K]=Var(K)=\lambda. \]

If a tenant averages two credential-stuffing alerts per hour, the probability of at least one in an hour is (1-e^{-2}=0.8647). Real attacks cluster, so empirical variance often exceeds the mean. A negative-binomial model or hierarchical rate can represent overdispersion. Always include exposure: ten alerts among 100 logins differs from ten among a million.

Exponential waiting time

The waiting time (T) in a Poisson process is exponential:

\[ P(T>t)=e^{-\lambda t},\qquad E[T]=1/\lambda. \]

Its memoryless property rarely describes remediation perfectly: old vulnerabilities may be systematically harder, violating constant hazard. Survival methods can model time-varying hazard and right censoring.

Normal, lognormal, and heavy tails

The normal distribution is symmetric and useful for additive measurement error and sampling means. It is often poor for positive skewed latency or loss. If (log X\sim N(\mu,\sigma^2)), then (X) is lognormal with median (e^\mu) and mean (e^{\mu+\sigma^2/2}); the mean exceeds the median.

File sizes, response times, and incident costs may be heavy-tailed. A power-law tail satisfies approximately (P(X>x)\propto x^{-\alpha}) above a threshold. Do not declare a power law from a straight line on a log-log chart; compare alternative tail models and estimate the threshold. Heavy tails make sample means unstable and extreme scenarios important.

Expectation, variance, and covariance

Expectation is probability-weighted average. Variance measures squared dispersion. Covariance

\[ Cov(X,Y)=E[(X-E[X])(Y-E[Y])] \]

captures linear co-movement and depends on scale. Correlation standardizes it to ([-1,1]). Neither establishes cause. Correlated detections may share a sensor, campaign, or label process.

Case File B: Estimation from a Sample

Suppose auditors randomly inspect 400 detector alerts and confirm 44 malicious files. Estimated precision is

\[ \hat p=44/400=0.11. \]

A point estimate without uncertainty invites false precision. The naive Wald interval, (hat p\pm1.96\sqrt{\hat p(1-\hat p)/n}), performs poorly near boundaries or with small samples. The Wilson interval has better coverage:

\[ \frac{\hat p+z^2/(2n)\pm z\sqrt{\hat p(1-\hat p)/n+z^2/(4n^2)}}{1+z^2/n}. \]

For 44 of 400 at 95%, it is approximately [0.083, 0.145]. This is a confidence interval: over repeated samples, 95% of intervals built by the procedure cover the fixed parameter. It is not a 95% probability statement about this fixed (p).

A Bayesian model with (p\sim Beta(1,1)) yields posterior (Beta(45,357)). A 95% credible interval allows the direct probability interpretation conditional on model and prior. Similar numerical intervals do not make the philosophies identical.

Prediction intervals are different

A confidence interval concerns a parameter such as mean alert volume. A prediction interval concerns a future observation and includes process variation. If daily false alerts are Poisson with uncertain rate, tomorrow’s predictive distribution is wider than uncertainty about the mean rate. Staffing from a confidence interval for the mean understates queue spikes.

Bootstrap and robust summaries

For a complicated statistic, resample observations with replacement, recompute the statistic, and use the bootstrap distribution. Resampling must match dependence: sessions from the same account or days from the same campaign may need cluster or block bootstrap. Median and trimmed means reduce sensitivity to extreme times, but the choice must match the operational question; the tail may be exactly what incident response cares about.

Case File C: Did the New Rule Help?

Before a rule change, 120 of 10,000 reviewed alerts were confirmed malicious. Afterward, 162 of 10,000 were confirmed. The observed precision difference is (0.0162-0.0120=0.0042), or 0.42 percentage points.

Under the null (p_1=p_2), pooled proportion is (282/20,000=0.0141). Standard error is

\[ SE=\sqrt{0.0141(1-0.0141)(1/10000+1/10000)}=0.001667. \]

Thus (z=0.0042/0.001667=2.52), with two-sided (p\approx0.0118). At a predeclared 0.05 level, this rejects equality. It does not prove the rule caused improvement: time, campaigns, reviewers, and sampling may differ. Nor does significance establish importance. The change adds about 42 confirmed cases per 10,000 reviewed alerts; whether that matters depends on misses, queue cost, and displacement.

Power is the probability of rejecting the null at a specified true effect. Rare outcomes require large samples. Designing for an implausibly large effect produces an underpowered study. Running hundreds of segment tests inflates false discoveries; use prespecified hypotheses, family-wise or false-discovery controls, and independent validation. Exploratory findings should be labeled exploratory.

Permutation testing can compare groups with fewer distributional assumptions: shuffle treatment labels under exchangeability and measure how often differences are at least as extreme. If assignment was not exchangeable, permutation does not repair confounding.

Bayesian Update Lab

This program reproduces the base-rate calculation, Wilson interval, beta posterior, and likelihood-ratio update.

from math import sqrt
from scipy.stats import beta

prevalence = 0.001
sensitivity = 0.99
specificity = 0.99
posterior = sensitivity * prevalence / (
    sensitivity * prevalence + (1 - specificity) * (1 - prevalence)
)
print(f"P(malware|alert)={posterior:.4f}")

n = 400; successes = 44; z = 1.96
phat = successes / n
center = (phat + z*z/(2*n)) / (1 + z*z/n)
half = z * sqrt(phat*(1-phat)/n + z*z/(4*n*n)) / (1 + z*z/n)
print(f"Wilson95=[{center-half:.3f}, {center+half:.3f}]")

lo, hi = beta.ppf([0.025, 0.975], 1 + successes, 1 + n - successes)
print(f"Beta posterior mean={(1+successes)/(2+n):.3f}")
print(f"Credible95=[{lo:.3f}, {hi:.3f}]")

odds = posterior / (1 - posterior)
odds *= 20
print(f"P(malware|alert,sandbox)={odds/(1+odds):.4f}")

Expected output:

P(malware|alert)=0.0902
Wilson95=[0.083, 0.144]
Beta posterior mean=0.112
Credible95=[0.083, 0.144]
P(malware|alert,sandbox)=0.6647

The uniform beta prior adds one pseudo-success and one pseudo-failure. In production, prior choice should reflect historical exchangeability and be tested for sensitivity. A posterior is only as credible as its likelihood and data-generating assumptions.

Monte Carlo Lab: Will the Queue Overflow?

Analytical expectations hide operational tails. Simulate daily traffic, malware arrivals, detections, false alerts, and analyst capacity. A beta distribution represents uncertainty in the false-positive rate rather than pretending it is known exactly.

import numpy as np

rng = np.random.default_rng(20260820)
days = 100_000
files = 100_000
capacity = 1_150
malicious = rng.binomial(files, 0.001, days)
true_alerts = rng.binomial(malicious, 0.99)
false_positive_rate = rng.beta(100, 9900, days)
false_alerts = rng.binomial(files - malicious, false_positive_rate)
alerts = true_alerts + false_alerts

print(f"mean_alerts={alerts.mean():.1f}")
print(f"p95_alerts={np.quantile(alerts, .95):.0f}")
print(f"overflow_probability={(alerts > capacity).mean():.3f}")
print(f"mean_true_alerts={true_alerts.mean():.1f}")

Expected output for NumPy 2.5.2:

mean_alerts=1098.6
p95_alerts=1277
overflow_probability=0.302
mean_true_alerts=99.0

The expected queue is below capacity, yet overflow occurs about 30% of days because the false-positive rate is uncertain. Simulation is not prophecy. Vary prevalence, correlation, campaign bursts, sensor outages, and analyst service time. Model validation includes checking whether simulated components reproduce historical marginal distributions and dependence.

Sampling, Bias, and the Law of Large Numbers

For independent identically distributed observations with finite expectation, sample averages converge toward the expectation. More data reduces random error; it does not remove systematic bias. A million adjudicated alerts can estimate the precision of reviewed alerts tightly while saying little about undetected malware.

Selection bias arises because current policy determines review. Verification bias occurs when only positives receive definitive testing. Survivorship bias excludes destroyed or unenrolled devices. Measurement bias enters when engines share labels. Concept drift changes (P(Y\mid X)); prior-probability shift changes (P(Y)). Security data violate IID assumptions through campaigns, tenants, repeated entities, and adaptive attackers.

Random sampling from the target population is the cleanest remedy for prevalence estimation. Stratified sampling improves precision for rare or important groups when weights are retained. Cluster sampling may be cheaper but increases variance. Convenience samples require a narrower claim.

Statistical and Operational Significance

A tiny precision increase may be statistically detectable at massive scale but operationally irrelevant. A modest reduction in critical ransomware misses may be valuable despite wide uncertainty. Report absolute effects, relative effects, intervals, denominators, and translated consequences.

Decision makers also need robustness. Does the conclusion change if prevalence is half the estimate? If false-positive cost doubles? If one campaign is removed? Sensitivity analysis exposes conclusions balanced on fragile assumptions. “Not statistically significant” means the study did not reject its null; it does not prove equivalence. Equivalence and noninferiority require margins defined before seeing results.

Dependence Is Not a Footnote

Many textbook formulas assume independent trials. Security observations cluster within users, hosts, tenants, days, and campaigns. Ten thousand files from one outbreak do not provide the same information as ten thousand independent families. Ignoring dependence makes standard errors too small and evidence look stronger than it is.

Match analysis to the sampling unit. Use cluster-robust uncertainty when assignment is individual but outcomes correlate within organizations; random effects or hierarchical models when group variation is itself important; and block resampling for time dependence. Report the number of independent clusters, not only the row count. With very few clusters, asymptotic corrections can remain unreliable, so design-based randomization inference or conservative aggregation may be preferable.

Calibration uncertainty deserves the same care. Reliability diagrams built from tiny bins can look erratic or deceptively perfect. Report bin counts, use adaptive or prespecified bins, and complement plots with proper scoring rules such as log loss or Brier score. Recalibration can repair probability mapping under stable ranking, but it cannot recover missed features, selection bias, or a changed target. When prevalence shifts, intercept adjustment may help; when class-conditional behavior changes, fresh labeled evidence is necessary. Treat every numeric probability as a claim tied to a population, time window, and adjudication process.
