Constraint change three. During an incident, leadership asks to revoke every session over 0.7.

Ask what 0.7 means and show action-specific calibration. A step-up threshold is not a revocation threshold. A temporary scoped rule may revoke sessions descending from a known token family, with owner and expiration. Do not convert an ambiguous population score into emergency authority.

Weak answers center impossible travel, merge humans and services, ignore token lineage, or discuss precision without recovery. Staff answers design state and action tiers. Principal answers establish prohibited insider-risk uses, regional contracts, expiring emergency policy, and accountable ownership.

Key Takeaways

  • Evaluate trust throughout sessions and at authorization boundaries, not only login.
  • Prefer protocol-grounded evidence to unstable novelty signals.
  • Separate human, workload, and emergency identities.
  • Insider-risk analytics must target approved acts, minimize data, and preserve human review.
  • Measure interrupted compromise together with friction and safe recovery.

Chapter 27: Network, Endpoint, Cloud, and Application Analytics

An Investigation Is a Join Across Partial Witnesses

No telemetry domain tells the whole story. A network flow sees endpoints and bytes but often not the process or authenticated user. Endpoint telemetry sees process ancestry but may lose traffic after a host sensor fails. Cloud audit records control-plane requests but not necessarily what happened inside a workload. Application logs know business objects and authorization outcomes but may not identify the originating container. Kubernetes audit records API decisions while runtime activity occurs elsewhere.

Cross-domain analytics therefore should not begin with an “entity risk score.” It begins with a claim that can be supported or contradicted by independent witnesses. Consider: “A stolen developer session was used to create a cloud credential, deploy a workload, and exfiltrate customer records.” The useful output is a time-ordered evidence bundle showing subject, process, workload, request, and network destination, with uncertainty at every join.

Correlation is not ordinary equality. Clocks differ, identifiers are reused, NAT collapses hosts, containers are ephemeral, and collectors duplicate or delay events. A reliable investigation timeline distinguishes observed facts from inferred links and records why each inference was made.

Domain-Specific Evidence

Network flow and encrypted metadata

A flow record should contain observation start/end, source and destination addresses and ports, transport, bytes and packets in each direction, sensor, sampling rate, network zone, and translated addresses when lawful and available. TLS metadata may include version, SNI or privacy-approved hostname category, certificate fingerprint, ALPN, and handshake outcome. JA3-like fingerprints can support hunting but are neither stable identities nor maliciousness labels; libraries and middleboxes create collisions.

Useful derived values include duration, byte ratio, packet-size statistics, fan-out, failed-connection rate, periodicity, and destination novelty. For event times \(t_1,\dots,t_n\), beacon regularity can be summarized by coefficient of variation

\[ CV=\frac{\operatorname{sd}(t_i-t_{i-1})}{\operatorname{mean}(t_i-t_{i-1})}. \]

Low \(CV\) is evidence of periodicity, not command-and-control: health checks and agents are periodic too. Destination reputation should retain observation date because domains and addresses change ownership.

Endpoint process trees

Process analytics require boot-scoped identity. A PID alone is unsafe because operating systems reuse it. A process key should combine device, boot identifier, PID, and start time. Record executable path and hash, signer, command-line representation subject to privacy controls, parent process key, user or workload identity, integrity level, and termination time.

Sequences often carry more meaning than individual names. winword -> powershell -> rundll32 is different from a management agent invoking PowerShell from an approved path, even if each binary is common. Represent ancestry as typed edges and preserve missing-parent status. If collection begins after process start, inventing a root creates false confidence.

Cloud control plane

Cloud events need provider, account/project/subscription, region, principal, credential/session, API operation, resource, source context, user agent, request parameters with secret redaction, response status, policy decision, and request ID. Separate control-plane creation from data-plane use. Creating an access key and using it are related but distinct evidence.

High-value patterns include disabling logs before privilege changes, creating credentials followed by new-region use, modifying trust policies, snapshot sharing, and unusual role assumption. Baseline by automation identity and deployment pipeline; infrastructure-as-code produces legitimate bursts that look extraordinary beside human administration.

Application and API activity

Application logs supply business semantics: tenant, authenticated principal, session, route template, object type, authorization decision, response class, records returned, and trace identifier. Never aggregate by raw URL when it embeds customer IDs. API abuse may appear as object enumeration, pagination manipulation, unusual error transitions, or a token exercising a permission it historically held but never used.

Kubernetes and workload identity

Kubernetes audit events identify user, groups, verb, object reference, namespace, request and response status, source IPs, stage, audit ID, and impersonation. Join pod UID—not merely pod name—to container runtime, image digest, node, service account, and cloud workload identity. Names are reusable; UIDs and validity intervals prevent yesterday's pod from being joined to today's traffic.

A Canonical Evidence Envelope

Do not flatten every source into a lowest-common-denominator table. Preserve source payloads and normalize only fields needed for correlation:

{
  "event_id":"cloud:01J5...",
  "event_type":"cloud.credential.create",
  "observed_at":"2026-08-20T15:04:12.882Z",
  "ingested_at":"2026-08-20T15:04:15.104Z",
  "producer":"aws-cloudtrail",
  "tenant_id":"acme",
  "actor":{"type":"human","id":"u-17","session_id":"s-91"},
  "object":{"type":"access_key","id":"key-tokenized-4"},
  "trace":{"request_id":"req-8","trace_id":null},
  "network":{"source_ip":"198.51.100.8","asn":64520},
  "source_schema":"cloudtrail-1.09",
  "normalizer_version":"3.4.1",
  "payload_ref":"object://immutable/evidence/01J5..."
}

This envelope resembles CloudEvents in separating event identity, source, type, subject, and time; OpenTelemetry supplies trace/span conventions for instrumented applications; ECS provides a broad field vocabulary. None removes the need for local semantics. user.id, for example, can mean an employee, customer, operating-system account, or workload. Record namespace and identity type.

Correlation as Bounded Inference

The strongest join uses a propagated trace or request ID. Next are cryptographically or platform-bound identifiers such as session ID, pod UID, or cloud request ID. Weaker joins use shared device, IP, user agent, and time. Every inferred link should carry a method and confidence.

If source \(A\) has clock-error bound \(\epsilon_A\) and source \(B\) has \(\epsilon_B\), events can be temporally compatible when

\[ [t_A-\epsilon_A,t_A+\epsilon_A]\cap[t_B-\epsilon_B,t_B+\epsilon_B]\ne\varnothing. \]

For an expected causal delay \([d_{min},d_{max}]\), shift the second interval accordingly. A fixed “within five minutes” join hides whether clocks are accurate to milliseconds or hours. Estimate skew from known paired events—load-balancer request IDs and application traces, for example—and monitor it per source.

Candidate-link confidence can be an auditable log-likelihood ratio:

\[ \ell(A,B)=\log\frac{P(M\mid same)}{P(M\mid different)}, \]

where \(M\) contains identifier match, temporal compatibility, topology, and expected sequence. Do not pretend independence among IP, subnet, and ASN. For investigations, expose the components rather than only the combined value.

SQL for a Point-in-Time Timeline

The following SQLite-compatible query constructs one evidence timeline using explicit keys. It avoids a many-to-many time-only join.

WITH scoped_sessions AS (
  SELECT session_id, subject_id, device_id, started_at, ended_at
  FROM identity_sessions
  WHERE subject_id = :subject_id
    AND started_at < :investigation_end
    AND COALESCE(ended_at, :investigation_end) >= :investigation_start
),
timeline AS (
  SELECT e.occurred_at, 'endpoint' AS domain, e.event_id,
         e.process_key AS object_id, s.session_id, 'device_session' AS link_method
  FROM endpoint_events e
  JOIN scoped_sessions s ON s.device_id = e.device_id
   AND e.occurred_at >= s.started_at
   AND e.occurred_at < COALESCE(s.ended_at, :investigation_end)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT c.occurred_at, 'cloud', c.event_id, c.resource_id,
         c.session_id, 'session_id'
  FROM cloud_events c JOIN scoped_sessions s ON s.session_id = c.session_id
  UNION ALL
  SELECT a.occurred_at, 'application', a.event_id, a.object_id,
         a.session_id, 'session_id'
  FROM application_events a JOIN scoped_sessions s ON s.session_id = a.session_id
)
SELECT occurred_at, domain, event_id, object_id, session_id, link_method
FROM timeline
ORDER BY occurred_at, domain, event_id;

Network flows need a separate mapping from device interface and validity interval; joining every flow by a shared public IP would be indefensible. All tables should retain ingested_at so investigators can tell whether an event was available to the original detector or only arrived later.

Safe Runnable Lab: Build an Evidence Timeline

This standard-library lab correlates synthetic records using explicit session and pod identifiers, then asserts the hypothesized sequence.

from datetime import datetime, timezone

def instant(value):
    return datetime.fromisoformat(value.replace("Z", "+00:00"))

events = [
 {"id":"e1","time":"2026-08-20T15:00:00Z","domain":"endpoint",
  "kind":"shell_start","session":"s91","pod":None},
 {"id":"c1","time":"2026-08-20T15:02:00Z","domain":"cloud",
  "kind":"credential_create","session":"s91","pod":None},
 {"id":"k1","time":"2026-08-20T15:05:00Z","domain":"kubernetes",
  "kind":"pod_create","session":"s91","pod":"pod-uid-7"},
 {"id":"a1","time":"2026-08-20T15:07:00Z","domain":"application",
  "kind":"bulk_export","session":None,"pod":"pod-uid-7"},
 {"id":"n1","time":"2026-08-20T15:08:00Z","domain":"network",
  "kind":"large_egress","session":None,"pod":"pod-uid-7"},
 {"id":"noise","time":"2026-08-20T15:06:00Z","domain":"network",
  "kind":"large_egress","session":None,"pod":"pod-uid-other"},
]

def correlated(seed_session, rows):
    selected = {r["id"] for r in rows if r["session"] == seed_session}
    pods = {r["pod"] for r in rows if r["id"] in selected and r["pod"]}
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for row in rows:
            if row["id"] not in selected and row["pod"] in pods:
                selected.add(row["id"]); changed = True
                if row["pod"]: pods.add(row["pod"])
    return sorted((r for r in rows if r["id"] in selected),
                  key=lambda r: (instant(r["time"]), r["id"]))

timeline = correlated("s91", events)
kinds = [row["kind"] for row in timeline]
print(" -> ".join(kinds))
assert kinds == ["shell_start", "credential_create", "pod_create",
                 "bulk_export", "large_egress"]
assert "noise" not in {row["id"] for row in timeline}
assert all(instant(timeline[i]["time"]) <= instant(timeline[i+1]["time"])
           for i in range(len(timeline)-1))

Expected output is shell_start -> credential_create -> pod_create -> bulk_export -> large_egress. The unrelated flow shares time and event type but not pod identity, so it is excluded. A production implementation should store each link as an edge with link_method, confidence, and evidence references; transitive expansion must have domain and time bounds to avoid swallowing an entire tenant.

From Timeline to Detection

Once evidence is linked, detection can operate on sequences rather than additive points. A finite-state rule for the constructed case might require credential creation by an interactive identity, workload creation using the credential within 15 minutes, sensitive export by that workload, and egress above a tenant-relative threshold. Each transition has a maximum delay and compatible identity relation.

Entity aggregation should preserve mechanisms. Summing “endpoint severity 40 + network severity 30 + cloud severity 50” creates a false numerical precision and lets ten weak correlated alerts outweigh one protocol violation. Prefer a small set of reasoned hypotheses with supporting/contradicting evidence. Deduplicate downstream alerts into an investigation keyed by incident hypothesis, not merely actor.

For streaming, event-time state must tolerate late arrivals. A watermark closes a window operationally, not epistemically; late evidence may revise a timeline. Emit revision numbers and avoid destructive overwrites. Analysts need to know that version 3 added a cloud event received 47 minutes late.

Production Failure Analysis

Identifier collision. PID, container name, username, and IP are reusable. Use boot IDs, UIDs, namespaces, and validity intervals.

Clock-skew fiction. A generous time window creates plausible but false stories. Measure per-source skew and show temporal uncertainty.

Cardinality explosion. Joining shared IPs or generic service accounts produces millions of links. Require stronger keys or cap fan-out and label ambiguity.

Normalization loss. Flattening source payloads discards request parameters needed later. Keep immutable raw evidence with access controls and retention.

Sensor-selective truth. Managed endpoints have rich evidence while unmanaged workloads appear quiet. Report coverage and never interpret missing telemetry as benign.

Duplicate cascades. Retries and multi-stage audit records multiply one action. Deduplicate with source IDs and documented stage semantics.

Collection-induced outage. Verbose application or Kubernetes auditing can overload systems or leak secrets. Redact at source, sample only where justified, and load-test policies.

Cross-tenant leakage. Correlation stores are powerful. Enforce tenant predicates in storage and service authorization, not only UI filters.

Operating a Correlation Pipeline

Each producer needs a measurable contract. Completeness can be approximated through sequence numbers, expected heartbeats, or comparison with an independent control-plane counter. Freshness should be measured as both source delay and pipeline delay: observed_at - occurred_at captures producer behavior, while available_at - observed_at captures transport and processing. Combining them into one latency hides where remediation belongs. Track p50, p95, and p99 by source, region, tenant class, and event type.

Schema changes should enter through versioned adapters and golden fixtures. A source field renamed from principalId to a nested object can silently null an identity join while event volume remains healthy. Contract tests should assert semantics: a known role-assumption fixture resolves the expected actor; a pod recreation generates a new UID; a denied API action remains denied after normalization. Preserve unknown enum values rather than mapping them to a familiar category.

Correlation rules need replayable versions. Store the normalized event IDs, rule version, state-machine transition, link methods, and window bounds for every emitted investigation. A rule edit should run against a fixed historical corpus and report changed cases, not only unit-test success. Because historical raw data may be sensitive or expensive, maintain small de-identified golden traces for common and adversarial sequences, plus access-controlled sampled replays for release review.

Queue behavior is part of validation. Measure how many source alerts consolidate into each investigation, how often separate incidents are incorrectly merged, and how often analysts split a case. Merge errors are asymmetric: over-merging creates an incoherent mega-incident; under-merging repeats work and hides a campaign. Provide reversible merge/split operations and feed those corrections into rule review without treating every analyst edit as ground truth.

Response automation should attach to verified transitions, not the mere existence of a cross-domain story. A known compromised token creating a credential may justify token revocation; a probabilistic IP/time link should not terminate a production workload. The investigation object should state which actions are permitted by which evidence class. If a required source becomes stale, keep the partial timeline, downgrade the hypothesis, and disable only dependent automation.

Retention tiers can reduce cost and exposure. Keep normalized envelopes and link edges for the investigation horizon; retain high-cardinality payloads for shorter, source-specific periods; preserve legal or incident evidence through explicit holds. Derived timelines must point to payload availability so an old explanation does not promise evidence already deleted. Hashes can verify integrity, but a hash of deleted evidence does not make the explanation independently reviewable.

Sources and Further Reading

  • OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions. Trace and span conventions can provide strong application links, but security fields and identity namespaces still require explicit local contracts. https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/
  • CloudEvents Specification. Its event envelope supports interoperable routing without requiring destructive flattening of domain payloads. https://github.com/cloudevents/spec
  • MITRE ATT&CK Data Sources. ATT&CK connects behaviors to observable components and helps expose coverage gaps; it is not a guarantee that a listed sensor observes every implementation. https://attack.mitre.org/datasources/
  • Kubernetes Auditing Documentation. Audit stages, policy levels, and request/response capture explain both the analytical value and the performance/privacy cost of Kubernetes evidence. https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/debug/debug-cluster/audit/
  • Elastic Common Schema. ECS offers useful shared names across domains; teams must still preserve source semantics, validity, and identity type. https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/ecs/current/ecs-reference.html

Interview Practicum

Scenario: Correlation When a Sensor Disappears.

Prompt. A customer reports that a developer account created a credential, deployed a pod, and exported data. Design a real-time cross-domain detector and an investigation view.

Ask which identifiers propagate, source latency/skew, retention, workload identity mapping, sensitive application actions, expected automation, and response authority.

Worked Answer

Propose canonical envelopes plus immutable payloads; build explicit session, request, pod UID, and workload-identity links; represent the hypothesis as a bounded state machine; emit an evidence graph and ordered timeline. Backtest point-in-time and measure confirmed-hypothesis precision, stage coverage, time to coherent evidence, duplicate investigations, and analyst correction rate.

Follow-Up Questions and Answers

Midstream constraint. Endpoint telemetry is unavailable on developer laptops for 90 days.

Do not claim equivalent coverage. Start the sequence at identity/cloud evidence, require stronger session and phishing-resistant authentication context, and label endpoint stage unknown. Increase audit sampling and consider a narrow preventive control on credential creation. Report the exact attacks that are no longer observable, such as local process ancestry.

Second constraint. Network telemetry is sampled 1:100 and NAT mappings are retained only one hour.

Use network evidence as corroboration, not required identity proof. Correct volume estimates only where sampling design supports it; retain uncertainty. Capture approved workload-to-flow mapping within the hour, aggregate privacy-preserving destination categories, and allow the detector to conclude “export observed, egress unconfirmed.”

Third constraint. Platform engineering says full Kubernetes request bodies add unacceptable API-server load.

Select audit levels by high-risk verbs and resources, exclude secret bodies, and measure policy overhead in a canary. Rely on object references, actor, verb, response, audit ID, and deployment provenance. The answer is a coverage/cost decision, not “log everything.”

Weak answers join on IP and time, flatten all logs into one score, or treat absent sensors as negative evidence. Staff answers reason about identifiers, clocks, state, and revision. Principal answers negotiate minimum viable telemetry, quantify residual blind spots, and move controls to boundaries that remain observable.

Key Takeaways

  • Cross-domain analytics builds evidence for hypotheses; it does not merely sum alerts.
  • Preserve domain payloads while normalizing a small correlation envelope.
  • Prefer propagated and platform-bound identifiers; time/IP joins are weaker inferences.
  • Model clock error, late data, identifier validity, and timeline revisions explicitly.
  • Missing sensors reduce what can be claimed and may justify moving controls to observable boundaries.

Chapter 28: Graph Analytics for Attack Paths

An Attack Path Is a Satisfiable Program

A security graph is not valuable because it draws many arrows. It is valuable when it can answer a counterfactual: if an attacker controls this principal under these conditions, which protected assets become reachable, why, and which change breaks the most credible paths?

Ordinary graph reachability is too permissive. An identity may belong to a group only during one interval; a role may require MFA; an exploit may apply only to a vulnerable image version; a network route may permit traffic in one direction; two permissions may need to be exercised in sequence. A reported path is credible only when its edges are simultaneously valid and its prerequisites are satisfiable. Treating all edges as timeless produces attack paths that never existed.

The graph is heterogeneous. Nodes include people, service principals, groups, roles, credentials, workloads, hosts, applications, data stores, vulnerabilities, and controls. Edges include membership, trust, assume-role, owns, can-read, can-write, can-execute, exposed-to, runs-on, vulnerable-to, and blocked-by. Each type has different semantics. A shortest path across untyped edges is usually a shortest explanation of the data model, not attacker effort.

Schema: Facts, Validity, and Preconditions

A compact relational representation is easier to test than an opaque graph import:

CREATE TABLE graph_nodes (
  tenant_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  node_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  node_type TEXT NOT NULL,
  criticality INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  properties_json TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, node_id)
);

CREATE TABLE graph_edges (
  tenant_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  edge_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  src_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  dst_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  edge_type TEXT NOT NULL,
  valid_from TEXT NOT NULL,
  valid_to TEXT,
  confidence REAL NOT NULL CHECK (confidence >= 0 AND confidence <= 1),
  precondition_json TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  evidence_ref TEXT NOT NULL,
  observed_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, edge_id)
);

Edges are claims with evidence, not eternal truth. valid_from and valid_to describe the world; observed_at describes when the system learned it. Both are required for historical reconstruction and point-in-time evaluation. A scanner result should connect a workload instance or image digest to a vulnerability with version evidence. A role edge should carry conditions such as external ID, source principal, MFA, session tag, or namespace.

Negative and control facts also matter. A firewall deny, permissions boundary, explicit deny, or non-exportable key can invalidate a candidate path. Absence of an allow edge is not necessarily a deny when collection is incomplete. Record coverage so traversal can return unknown instead of quietly treating missing data as safe or exploitable.

Traversal Semantics

Define an attacker state \(q=(K,C,t)\), where \(K\) is controlled principals/resources, \(C\) is acquired capabilities, and \(t\) is evaluation time. An edge \(e\) is traversable when:

\[ valid_e(t)\land prereq_e(C)\land scope_e(K)\land \neg blocked_e(t). \]

Traversal applies a state transition \(q' = T_e(q)\), perhaps adding a credential, execution capability, or resource control. This captures an important distinction: reading a secret grants a capability that can enable a later assume-role edge; merely being adjacent to the secret node does not.

For static IAM analysis, typed reachability may suffice. For exploit paths, use constrained search over state. Bound path length and prevent repeated states, not merely repeated nodes, because revisiting a node with a new capability can be meaningful. Keep the transition library small and reviewed. Overly expressive preconditions make results impossible to validate.

Centrality, Chokepoints, and Blast Radius

Degree finds hubs, but directory groups and scanners are often benign hubs. Betweenness centrality

\[ C_B(v)=\sum_{s\ne v\ne t}\frac{\sigma_{st}(v)}{\sigma_{st}} \]

counts the fraction of shortest paths passing through \(v\). It can identify chokepoints, but only under the chosen edge weights and path definition. In security, the most important path may not be shortest, and thousands of near-duplicate group paths can dominate.

Blast radius is more actionable: given initial control \(S\), count or value critical assets reachable under valid transitions. Weighting asset value yields

\[ BR(S)=\sum_{a\in Reach(S)}V(a). \]

For remediation edge \(e\), marginal path reduction is \(\Delta_e=BR(S)-BR_{-e}(S)\). This estimates leverage, not guaranteed risk reduction. Removing one group membership may break 300 enumerated paths that all represent the same underlying privilege. Report unique protected assets and independent mechanisms as well as raw path count.

Communities can expose trust zones that do not match intended architecture. Motifs—user to group to role, workload to secret to cloud account—can encode known escalation patterns. Their value comes from typed semantics, not graph-theory novelty.

Ranking Paths Without Fake Probability

Suppose each edge has estimated success \(p_e\), detection probability \(d_e\), time cost \(c_e\), and confidence \(r_e\). A candidate score might be

\[ J(P)=\sum_{e\in P}-\log(p_e)+\lambda\sum c_e+gamma\sum d_e+eta\sum -\log(r_e). \]

Lower is easier or better supported. This additive form implicitly treats factors as separable; shared credentials, controls, and evidence violate independence. Use it for ranking and sensitivity analysis, never as an exact breach probability. Show how rankings change when uncertain weights vary.

A practical priority should include starting-point exposure, target criticality, path feasibility, evidence freshness, existing detections, and remediation leverage. Internet exposure is not a universal starting point: phishing, insider access, vendor compromise, and workload compromise create other starts. Maintain scenario-specific rankings.

Graph embeddings and graph neural networks can rank nodes or missing links, but they introduce identity leakage, temporal leakage, and difficult explanations. A random edge split lets the same identity neighborhood appear in train and test. Evaluate on later graph snapshots and new entities. Begin with typed traversal and transparent path features; add learned representations only for measurable lift on adjudicated tasks.

A Unique Architecture for Temporal Truth

flowchart LR
    S[Source snapshots<br/>IAM, CMDB, scanners, network policy] --> F[Versioned edge facts]
    F --> T[Temporal + prerequisite validator]
    T --> Q[Scenario search<br/>initial control and target]
    Q --> P[Candidate paths]
    P --> E[Evidence expansion<br/>why each hop works]
    E --> R[Edge-removal simulation]
    R --> C[Remediation choice]
    C --> S

The validator is the important component. It rejects edges outside the evaluation time, expands group and trust semantics, checks required capabilities, applies explicit denies, and records unknown coverage. Search and ranking should never bypass it.

Safe Runnable Lab: Temporal Privilege Paths

This standard-library lab finds feasible paths and simulates remediation. The graph is synthetic and contains no real cloud credentials.

from collections import defaultdict, deque

edges = [
 ("internet", "web", "exposed", 1.0),
 ("web", "web-role", "workload_identity", 1.0),
 ("web-role", "build-secret", "read_secret", 1.4),
 ("build-secret", "ci-role", "credential_for", 0.8),
 ("ci-role", "signing-key", "can_sign", 1.0),
 ("contractor", "dev-group", "member_of", 0.2),
 ("dev-group", "ci-role", "assume_role", 1.2),
 ("old-group", "signing-key", "can_sign", 0.1),  # expired
]
valid = {tuple(e[:3]) for e in edges if e[0] != "old-group"}

def paths(source, target, removed=None, cutoff=6):
    removed = removed or set()
    graph = defaultdict(list)
    costs = {}
    for src, dst, kind, cost in edges:
        key = (src, dst, kind)
        if key in valid and key not in removed:
            graph[src].append((dst, kind))
            costs[key] = cost
    queue = deque([(source, [source], [], 0.0)])
    found = []
    while queue:
        node, nodes, hops, cost = queue.popleft()
        if node == target:
            found.append((cost, nodes, hops)); continue
        if len(hops) >= cutoff: continue
        for nxt, kind in graph[node]:
            if nxt not in nodes:
                key = (node, nxt, kind)
                queue.append((nxt, nodes+[nxt], hops+[kind], cost+costs[key]))
    return sorted(found)

internet_paths = paths("internet", "signing-key")
contractor_paths = paths("contractor", "signing-key")
cut = {("dev-group", "ci-role", "assume_role")}
after_cut = paths("contractor", "signing-key", removed=cut)

print(internet_paths[0][1])
print(contractor_paths[0][1])
assert internet_paths[0][1] == ["internet", "web", "web-role",
                                "build-secret", "ci-role", "signing-key"]
assert contractor_paths[0][1] == ["contractor", "dev-group", "ci-role",
                                  "signing-key"]
assert after_cut == []
assert paths("old-group", "signing-key") == []

Expected output is the two asserted node lists. Removing dev-group -> ci-role eliminates the contractor path, while the expired edge never appears. The lab deliberately separates validity from topology. A production extension would represent prerequisites and capabilities explicitly and test that every explanatory hop has accessible source evidence.

Explainable Findings and Remediation Choice

A finding should read like a proof:

  1. The contractor is an active member of dev-group according to directory snapshot X.
  2. The group's trust policy can assume ci-role without MFA under policy version Y.
  3. ci-role can invoke signing with key Z under effective policy simulation.
  4. The key protects production release artifacts and has criticality 5.
  5. Removing membership M breaks this scenario and two other independent paths; removing public web exposure does not affect it.

Include evaluation time, source freshness, unknown checks, and alternative paths. Analysts should be able to replay the query. If an edge depends on a scanner heuristic, label it accordingly. If a control is assumed effective but untested, do not present it as a hard block.

Remediation is a constrained cut problem. The smallest cut may be operationally impossible—removing the CI role stops releases. Candidate actions have engineering cost, availability impact, owner, and time to implement. Optimize a portfolio:

\[ \max_{A}\;\text{critical reachability removed}(A) \quad\text{s.t.}\quad \sum_{a\in A}cost(a)\le B, \]

plus constraints preserving required business paths. Often the best action is to condition a trust edge, shorten credential lifetime, or add approval rather than delete access entirely.

Production Failure Analysis

Timeless edges. Historical grants and remediated vulnerabilities invent paths. Require validity intervals and snapshot reproducibility.

Path explosion. Nested groups and equivalent permissions create combinatorial duplicates. Canonicalize equivalent mechanisms, cap depth, and summarize by target and cut edge.

Missing negative controls. Ignoring explicit deny, network policy, MFA conditions, or key non-exportability overstates feasibility. Model them or return unknown.

Stale ownership and criticality. A graph can rank precisely against obsolete business context. Require owner attestation and freshness indicators.

Tenant boundary failure. One missing predicate can create cross-customer paths. Partition storage and authorize traversal at the service layer.

Scanner confidence laundering. Importing a vulnerability edge can make uncertain version matching look factual. Preserve scanner evidence and confidence.

Remediation metric gaming. Teams close many paths by deleting duplicate edges while critical reachability remains. Measure protected assets and independent scenarios.

Learned leakage. Embeddings memorize high-degree identities and graph snapshots. Use temporal/entity holdouts and compare against typed heuristics.

Testing the Graph as a Security Product

Graph correctness begins below path ranking. Adapter tests should prove that source facts become the right typed edges, validity intervals, and conditions. Semantic tests should cover nested groups, explicit deny precedence, cross-account trust, inherited Kubernetes roles, workload federation, secret versioning, and vulnerability applicability. Use tiny graphs with one intended answer; large realistic fixtures make a wrong path difficult to diagnose.

Metamorphic tests are particularly effective. Adding an unrelated node must not change existing reachability. Expiring an edge must remove every path that depends on it. Adding an explicit deny must not create a path. Renaming a display label must not change node identity. Duplicating equivalent evidence must not double path count. Removing a cut edge must not affect required paths that do not traverse it. These properties catch entire classes of ingestion and traversal defects.

For a sampled production finding, a reviewer should reproduce each hop in the authoritative system or its immutable snapshot. Track edge confirmation rate, invalid-path rate, unknown-control rate, stale-edge rate, time to owner identification, accepted remediation, and verified reachability after change. “Paths closed” is insufficient until the graph is refreshed and the same scenario search confirms that the target is no longer reachable—or explains an alternative.

Freshness has scenario-specific limits. A 24-hour CMDB delay may be acceptable for quarterly architecture review but dangerous for a just-in-time signing path. Give every edge type a freshness SLO and propagate the weakest freshness into the path explanation. If one critical edge is stale, rank may remain useful for investigation, but automation should stop. Snapshot publication should be atomic so a query never mixes half of yesterday's IAM state with half of today's.

Large graphs require engineering discipline rather than semantic shortcuts. Partition by tenant and administrative boundary, maintain reverse indexes from protected targets, precompute safe closures for stable group membership, and run bidirectional search from starts and targets. Cache results by graph snapshot and scenario, invalidating them on affected edge changes. Approximate algorithms may prioritize candidates, but final findings should pass exact semantic validation.

Treat the graph service as highly sensitive. It is an attacker roadmap containing privilege, vulnerability, and critical-asset relationships. Apply least privilege, purpose-bound query APIs, tenant isolation, result limits, audit trails, and controls on bulk export. Explanations shown to broad engineering audiences may need to redact unrelated identities while preserving remediation evidence. Protect source credentials and never let the analytics service acquire the privileges it is modeling merely for convenience.

Sources and Further Reading

  • BloodHound OpenGraph Documentation. BloodHound demonstrates how identity and privilege relations become traversable attack paths; production use still requires local temporal, control, and evidence semantics. https://bloodhound.specterops.io/opengraph/overview
  • Neo4j Graph Data Science Manual. Its path, centrality, community, and embedding algorithms are useful primitives, but algorithmic output inherits the graph projection's assumptions. https://neo4j.com/docs/graph-data-science/current/
  • NetworkX Algorithms Reference. NetworkX is appropriate for small reproducible fixtures and algorithm tests; it is not a substitute for production authorization or tenant isolation. https://networkx.org/documentation/stable/reference/algorithms/index.html
  • MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise Matrix. ATT&CK helps describe attacker transitions and evidence requirements, but techniques are not automatically graph edges without environment-specific prerequisites. https://attack.mitre.org/matrices/enterprise/
  • NIST SP 800-207. Zero Trust's resource and policy emphasis supports modeling conditional access and continuous verification instead of assuming network adjacency equals trust. https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/207/final

Interview Practicum

Scenario: The Best Cut Becomes Unavailable.

Prompt. A cloud company has 12 million privilege edges. Find and prioritize paths from internet-facing workloads and contractors to production signing keys, then recommend remediation.

Clarify graph semantics, snapshot history, starting scenarios, target inventory, cloud-policy evaluation, vulnerability evidence, control representation, maximum path depth, and remediation owners.

Worked Answer

Build versioned typed edges with validity and evidence; define attacker-state transitions; enumerate bounded feasible paths; rank by scenario exposure, feasibility, target value, freshness, and uncertainty; then simulate candidate cuts. Validate a sample hop by hop with IAM and service owners.

Follow-Up Questions and Answers

Midstream constraint. The apparent top cut—removing the CI role—would halt releases and is prohibited.

Reframe remediation as constrained optimization. Test narrower changes: remove contractor inheritance, require workload-bound federation, restrict signing conditions to approved pipeline claims, shorten sessions, or add a brokered signing service. Recompute reachability while asserting that the required release path remains. The goal is not minimum graph size; it is reduced unauthorized reachability with preserved business function.

Second constraint. IAM snapshots are daily, while just-in-time grants last 30 minutes.

Daily snapshots cannot prove or exclude those paths. Ingest grant lifecycle events or policy-decision logs with event time. Until then, label JIT traversal unknown and avoid claiming complete coverage. A temporary control can require signing-service logs and alert on non-pipeline callers at the target boundary.

Third constraint. Leadership wants to deploy a GNN because the graph is large.

Ask which supervised task and labels justify it. Scaling traversal is an engineering problem; it does not itself require learning. Partition by tenant/account, precompute reviewed relation closures, and use bidirectional bounded search. Consider a GNN only for a defined ranking task with temporal/entity holdouts, transparent baselines, and path-level explanations. Never allow a learned score to invent authorization semantics.

Weak answers run generic shortest path, multiply edge probabilities as independent, rank by degree, or optimize raw path count. Staff answers model prerequisites, temporal validity, evidence, and operational cuts. Principal answers protect required business paths, expose unknown coverage, choose target-boundary controls when graph data is late, and resist unjustified model complexity.

Key Takeaways

  • A credible attack path is a sequence of satisfiable, simultaneously valid transitions.
  • Typed edges need evidence, confidence, validity, preconditions, and control semantics.
  • Centrality and shortest path are heuristics; prioritize scenario reachability and remediation leverage.
  • Explain findings as replayable proofs and distinguish false, blocked, and unknown paths.
  • Optimize remediation under business constraints, then recompute reachability to verify the cut.

Chapter 29: Threat Intelligence and Exploit Prioritization

Exploitation Is a Forecast, Not a Severity Label

A scanner answers “what weakness is present?” A remediation program must decide which exposed weakness is likely to be used against this organization before it can be fixed. CVSS, EPSS, CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV), exploit reports, asset exposure, and business context describe different parts of that decision. Treating any one as the answer causes predictable mistakes.

CVSS v4.0 characterizes technical severity. EPSS estimates the probability that a published CVE will be exploited in the wild during the next 30 days. KEV says exploitation has occurred and assigns US federal remediation dates. None knows whether the vulnerable code path is reachable in your deployment, a control blocks it, or compromise reaches a material asset. The correct unit is therefore a time-stamped CVE–asset–deployment observation, not a CVE. The same CVE can require emergency work on an internet-facing identity gateway and normal maintenance on an isolated build host.

An Intelligence Contract That Preserves Evidence

Store observations separately from conclusions:

CREATE TABLE exploit_evidence (
  evidence_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  cve_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  observed_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  ingested_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  evidence_type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (evidence_type IN
    ('kev','epss','advisory','malware','honeypot','public_poc')),
  publisher TEXT NOT NULL,
  source_document TEXT NOT NULL,
  independent_group TEXT NOT NULL,
  supports_exploit INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (supports_exploit IN (0,1)),
  likelihood_ratio REAL,
  raw_value REAL,
  extraction_method TEXT NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE(cve_id,publisher,source_document,evidence_type)
);

CREATE TABLE deployment_observation (
  observation_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  observed_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  asset_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  cve_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  vulnerable_path INTEGER NOT NULL,
  internet_reachable INTEGER,       -- NULL means unknown
  control_state TEXT NOT NULL,
  asset_loss_usd REAL NOT NULL,
  remediation_hours REAL NOT NULL,
  inventory_source TEXT NOT NULL
);

independent_group prevents three feeds quoting one vendor bulletin from appearing to be three confirmations. observed_at says when an event happened; ingested_at says when the system could know it. Both are essential to honest backtests. STIX 2.1 is useful for exchanging indicators, sightings, relationships, and confidence, but STIX confidence is publisher metadata—not automatically a probability.

ATT&CK technique mappings add behavioral context. A CVE enabling External Remote Services (T1133) may support a campaign hypothesis, but the mapping is a typed, sourced relationship rather than proof that a campaign used that CVE. ATLAS plays an analogous role for attacks on machine-learning systems. Mappings should improve investigation and control selection, not become arbitrary score multipliers.

Bayesian Updating Without Circular Evidence

Let \(H\) mean “this CVE will be exploited against the relevant population during the decision horizon.” Starting with a point-in-time EPSS prior \(p_0\), prior odds are

\[ O(H)=\frac{p_0}{1-p_0}. \]

For conditionally independent evidence groups with calibrated likelihood ratios \(LR_g\):

\[ O(H\mid E)=O(H)\prod_g LR_g, \qquad P(H\mid E)=\frac{O(H\mid E)}{1+O(H\mid E)}. \]

A likelihood ratio is \(P(E\mid H)/P(E\mid\neg H)\), not an analyst’s 1–5 confidence. Estimate it from historical point-in-time observations. KEV inclusion usually deserves a strong positive ratio, but not infinity: “exploited somewhere” is not “will target this tenant.” A public proof of concept may add modest evidence. Four articles copied from the same researcher add one evidence group, not four.

Conditional independence is the fragile assumption. Reporting popularity creates another bias: famous vendors and dramatic CVEs receive more articles. Evaluate calibration by disclosure age, ecosystem size, and vendor prominence, and maintain low-attention challenge cases.

From Forecast to Action

Prioritization should minimize expected loss. For asset \(a\) and action \(d\):

\[ L(d)=p_{exploit}\,p_{reach}(a)\,p_{success}(a,d)\,C_{impact}(a)

  • C_{change}(a,d)+C_{delay}(d).

\]

p_reach represents whether the vulnerable path can be exercised. p_success accounts for remaining controls. C_change includes outage risk and labor. Emergency patching is justified when its expected reduction in compromise loss exceeds change cost. This is why “patch every critical CVSS in 24 hours” is incomplete: it omits exploitation likelihood, reachability, consequence, and patch risk.

Keep the components in the decision record:

{"decision_time":"2026-08-20T14:00:00Z","asset_id":"edge-idp-07",
 "cve_id":"CVE-20XX-9001","epss_asof":0.18,"posterior_exploit":0.798,
 "reachability":0.95,"impact_usd":900000,"change_cost_usd":18000,
 "action":"emergency_patch","evidence_groups":["kev:cisa","poc:r17"],
 "policy_version":"exploit-loss-v3"}

NLP as an evidence extractor

Advisory NLP should resolve product/version spans, distinguish “could allow exploitation” from “exploitation observed,” capture who asserted the claim and when, link to exact text, and cluster documents by common origin. “No evidence of exploitation” is not evidence of no exploitation. A language model may summarize a report, but consequential decisions must retain the underlying span and deterministic entity resolution.

Safe Lab: Evidence-Weighted Expected Avoided Loss

This synthetic lab deduplicates correlated evidence, updates odds, and chooses emergency work only when expected avoided loss exceeds change cost.

from dataclasses import dataclass
from math import prod

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Deployment:
    name: str; cve: str; epss: float; reach: float
    residual_after_patch: float; impact: float; change_cost: float

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Evidence:
    cve: str; origin: str; lr: float

def posterior(prior: float, items: list[Evidence], cve: str) -> float:
    if not 0 < prior < 1:
        raise ValueError("prior outside (0,1)")
    groups: dict[str, float] = {}
    for e in items:
        if e.cve == cve:
            groups[e.origin] = max(e.lr, groups.get(e.origin, 0.0))
    odds = prior / (1 - prior) * prod(groups.values())
    return odds / (1 + odds)

evidence = [
    Evidence("CVE-A", "researcher-17", 3.0),
    Evidence("CVE-A", "researcher-17", 2.5), # copied report
    Evidence("CVE-A", "cisa-kev", 6.0),
    Evidence("CVE-B", "public-poc", 1.4),
]
assets = [
    Deployment("edge-idp", "CVE-A", .18, .95, .30, 900_000, 18_000),
    Deployment("isolated-build", "CVE-A", .18, .02, .30, 120_000, 8_000),
    Deployment("marketing-site", "CVE-B", .04, .80, .40, 70_000, 9_000),
]
out = []
for a in assets:
    p = posterior(a.epss, evidence, a.cve)
    benefit = p * a.reach * a.impact * (1 - a.residual_after_patch)
    action = "emergency_patch" if benefit > a.change_cost else "normal_queue"
    out.append((a.name, round(p, 3), round(benefit), action))

expected = [
 ('edge-idp', .798, 477621, 'emergency_patch'),
 ('isolated-build', .798, 1341, 'normal_queue'),
 ('marketing-site', .055, 1852, 'normal_queue')]
assert out == expected, out
print(out)

Expected output is exactly expected. The shared CVE-A forecast produces different actions because local exposure and consequence differ. Without origin deduplication, duplicated reporting would create false certainty.

Production Failure Analysis

Future leakage. Joining today’s KEV and latest EPSS to old snapshots creates a clairvoyant backtest. Snapshot feeds and use only data ingested before each historical decision.

Invisible assets. An inner join between scanner and CMDB erases unmanaged assets. Publish join coverage. Distinguish “not reachable with recent evidence” from “reachability unknown”; missing must never become false.

Catalog bias. KEV is curated for a mission, not a random sample. “Not in KEV” is not a clean negative label. Use confirmed positives, delayed outcomes, reviewed samples, and positive-unlabeled methods where justified.

Queue shock. A feed update can move thousands of deployments across a threshold. Group common remediations, enforce engineering capacity, reserve an incident lane, and rank marginal avoided loss per hour. If EPSS becomes stale, fall back to explicitly degraded logic rather than silently reusing it forever.

Adversarial manipulation. Attackers can publish false exploit claims or poison sensors. Authenticate feeds, hash source material, separate extraction confidence from exploit evidence, and support removing a source followed by deterministic replay.

Evaluate the forecast with horizon-specific Brier score, calibration, and precision–recall. Evaluate the policy with expected loss avoided, emergency changes, incidents tied to vulnerable deployments, and remediation capacity. A calibrated forecast can still drive a poor policy if impact or patch-cost estimates are wrong.

Designing the Production Prioritizer

The production service should expose two APIs rather than one. A forecast API answers, for a CVE and timestamp, what exploitation probability and evidence were available. A decision API accepts a deployment observation, candidate actions, and policy version, then returns the chosen action and loss decomposition. This separation lets the threat-research team improve evidence fusion without owning business impact estimates, and lets asset owners dispute inventory or consequence without rewriting threat history.

Forecast features must be monotone in time: a document received tomorrow cannot change what was knowable today. Maintain append-only feed snapshots and a canonical CVE alias table. Reject records whose CVE identifier cannot be resolved, but retain them in a quarantine stream because pre-CVE exploitation reports are often valuable. When a CVE is later assigned, create a sourced alias event rather than rewriting the old document.

Asset context needs its own freshness rules. Network reachability may expire after hours; ownership might remain valid for weeks; business-impact tiers may be reviewed quarterly. Each field should carry measured_at, source, and expiry. The decision engine should abstain or widen its loss range when a critical input is stale. One global “data fresh” flag conceals the fact that different evidence decays at different rates.

Remediation grouping deserves explicit modeling. A package upgrade may remove five CVEs across 4,000 hosts with one tested change, while separately ranking every pair makes the work look impossibly large. Build candidate actions such as “upgrade base image X from digest A to B” and calculate the union of affected deployment losses, avoiding double counting when several CVEs lead to the same compromise path. Subtract testing, rollout, and expected outage cost once per action, not once per CVE.

Capacity constraints turn ranking into scheduling. Emergency windows, platform-team skills, freeze periods, dependency order, and rollback readiness can be represented as constraints. A simple greedy queue based on avoided loss per engineering hour is transparent and often adequate; integer optimization becomes useful when actions share prerequisites or maintenance windows. The optimizer must never invent precision: if impact is a broad range, solve optimistic and pessimistic schedules and surface actions stable across both.

An example decision review

Suppose an endpoint-management CVE has EPSS 0.12, a public exploit from one independent origin, and no KEV entry. It affects 6,000 laptops, but the vulnerable service is disabled on 5,400. The remaining 600 include 40 privileged administrator devices. The correct response is not a fleetwide priority score. Produce at least three deployment segments, verify configuration evidence, and compare actions: disable the service remotely, upgrade the agent, or isolate the administrator devices. A reversible configuration mitigation may dominate a risky emergency upgrade even though it does not “close” the scanner finding.

Now suppose the scanner cannot distinguish disabled from enabled services on 15% of laptops. The denominator is 6,000, not the 5,100 with confident configuration. Report the unknown segment and sample it. If sampling shows configuration data fails disproportionately on older, high-risk devices, random extrapolation is invalid; stratify by operating system and management health.

Evaluation data construction

Define the forecast horizon before collecting labels. For a 30-day forecast made daily, adjacent observations for one CVE share outcomes and cannot be treated as independent rows in an ordinary random split. Split by time and, for robustness, by CVE disclosure cohort. A positive label should cite an exploitation observation whose timestamp falls inside the horizon and whose source was not itself used as an input unless the evaluation explicitly measures assimilation speed.

Unobserved exploitation is not a confirmed negative. Honeypots and telemetry cover only parts of the internet, and reporting is selective. In addition to conventional metrics, estimate performance on high-observability strata and report label coverage. Sensitivity analysis can ask how calibration changes if a plausible fraction of unlabeled cases were exploited. This is more honest than presenting six decimal places from incomplete surveillance.

Policy evaluation should replay action availability as well as forecasts. A patch not published at decision time was not a feasible action. Likewise, a mitigation requiring a control the organization had not deployed cannot be credited retrospectively. Historical simulation should reconstruct inventory, controls, maintenance constraints, and labor capacity. Otherwise the model is evaluated in a fictional organization with perfect options.

Governance and human authority

Threat researchers should be able to flag a source as compromised, but removing it must produce a new evidence-policy version and an impact report listing changed decisions. Asset owners may correct reachability or impact with evidence and expiry, not by editing the threat probability. Incident commanders may override scheduling during active exploitation; the override record should state duration, scope, and reason.

Metrics create incentives. If vulnerability teams are measured by the number of KEV items closed, they may prioritize easy low-impact deployments and suppress hard exceptions. Pair timeliness with remaining expected exposure, unknown coverage, emergency-change harm, and recurrence. Review a random sample of “not affected” dispositions because that status can become a hiding place for inventory defects.

Finally, publish uncertainty in language operators can use: what is known, what is inferred, what is missing, and which new measurement would change the action. That is more actionable than a falsely precise percentile.

The service should also preserve rejected alternatives. Recording why mitigation lost to patching, or why acceptance lost to measurement, makes later incident review possible and prevents operators from reconstructing rationale from a score whose inputs have since changed.

Sources and Further Reading

  • FIRST, Exploit Prediction Scoring System. A daily probability forecast for exploitation in the next 30 days, complementary to severity. https://www.first.org/epss/
  • CISA, Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog. Strong curated exploitation evidence, but not an exhaustive negative-label boundary. https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog
  • FIRST, CVSS v4.0. Technical severity characteristics, including threat and environmental metrics; not organization-specific exploit forecasting. https://www.first.org/cvss/v4.0/
  • NIST, National Vulnerability Database. Normalized enrichment whose publication and revision times matter to point-in-time analysis. https://nvd.nist.gov/
  • OASIS, STIX 2.1. Exchange semantics for intelligence objects, relationships, and provenance. https://docs.oasis-open.org/cti/stix/v2.1/stix-v2.1.html
  • MITRE ATT&CK and ATLAS. Behavioral knowledge bases for enterprise and AI-system threats. https://attack.mitre.org/ and https://atlas.mitre.org/

Together these sources imply a layered system: CVSS describes characteristics, EPSS forecasts population exploitation, KEV adds observed-exploitation evidence, STIX carries sourced claims, and ATT&CK/ATLAS connect claims to behaviors. The organization still owns exposure, consequence, and intervention cost.

Interview Practicum

Scenario: The Forecast Changes Mid-Meeting.

Prompt. You have 140,000 CVE–asset pairs and capacity to remediate 2,000 per week. Design the service.

A strong candidate asks whether capacity counts hosts, packages, or change tickets; requests reachability, asset-loss tiers, maintenance windows, compensating controls, point-in-time feeds, exploit labels, and shared patches.

Worked Answer

The initial design builds time-stamped deployment observations, uses EPSS as a prior, groups independent evidence, estimates exposure and residual control effectiveness, then schedules common remediation actions by expected avoided loss per engineering hour.

Follow-Up Questions and Answers

Constraint change one: reachability is only 60% complete and weekly. Introduce reachable, recently verified unreachable, and unknown states. Use loss bounds for unknowns. Cases whose action changes across the bounds enter a measurement queue. Publish coverage as an SLI; do not claim risk fell when visibility disappeared.

Constraint change two: an identity appliance enters KEV Friday afternoon, but its patch has a 4% outage rate and downtime is forbidden before Monday. Compare weekend compromise loss with outage loss. Apply reversible controls—management-plane restriction, targeted detection, stronger authentication, and active hunting—then patch in an approved window with rollback. Do not reduce the threat score to rationalize the operational decision.

Principal probe: leadership wants one number. Report estimated exploitable exposure above the approved loss threshold, with an uncertainty range, the fraction actively mitigated, and age. Operators retain the components.

Weak answers sort only by CVSS or EPSS, add incompatible scales, treat KEV absence as a negative label, or convert NLP confidence directly into exploit probability.

Key Takeaways

  • CVSS severity, EPSS probability, KEV evidence, and local risk are different variables.
  • Prioritize time-stamped CVE–asset–deployment observations, not CVEs alone.
  • Bayesian updates require calibrated likelihood ratios and source-lineage deduplication.
  • Schedule interventions by expected avoided loss under real remediation capacity.
  • Preserve feed history, unknown exposure states, evidence spans, and policy versions.
  • Evaluate forecast calibration and downstream policy outcomes separately.

Chapter 30: Measuring the Quality of Security Findings

A Finding Is a Falsifiable Claim

A security finding is not high quality because a tool emitted it or called it critical. It is a claim containing an affected artifact and version, a weakness mechanism, a reachable trigger, an undesirable consequence, and evidence another investigator can reproduce. Accuracy, severity, exploitability, business impact, actionability, and novelty are separate axes. A true but unreachable weakness can be accurate and low priority; a duplicate can be correct yet add no queue value.

CREATE TABLE finding(
 finding_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, scanner_version TEXT NOT NULL,
 repository TEXT NOT NULL, commit_sha TEXT NOT NULL, artifact_uri TEXT NOT NULL,
 rule_id TEXT NOT NULL, cwe_id TEXT, source_span TEXT NOT NULL,
 sink_span TEXT, trace_hash TEXT, trigger_fixture TEXT,
 claimed_severity TEXT NOT NULL, confidence REAL CHECK(confidence BETWEEN 0 AND 1),
 emitted_at TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE adjudication(
 finding_id TEXT, reviewer_id TEXT, reviewed_at TEXT NOT NULL,
 verdict TEXT CHECK(verdict IN ('confirmed','refuted','inconclusive','duplicate','environment_blocked')),
 root_cause_id TEXT, reproducible INTEGER, reachable INTEGER,
 minutes_to_validate INTEGER, evidence_grade TEXT, rationale TEXT,
 PRIMARY KEY(finding_id,reviewer_id));

The explicit inconclusive and environment-blocked states prevent forced binary labels. Scanner and commit versions prevent a later code change from making an old finding appear irreproducible. Reviewer identity supports agreement analysis without pretending adjudicators are infallible.

Three Levels of Measurement

For reviewed claims, precision is \(TP/(TP+FP)\). Recall requires a denominator of weaknesses that should have been found; ordinary production output does not provide it. Seeded and curated corpora help, but NIST SARD and OWASP Benchmark are regression instruments, not estimates of prevalence in a company’s repositories.

Reproducibility must name its environment:

\[ R=\frac{\text{confirmed findings reproduced under pinned fixtures}} {\text{confirmed findings attempted under pinned fixtures}}. \]

A missing compiler or expired test credential is an environment block, not a false positive. Measure that rate separately.

For confidence \(p_i\) and binary adjudication \(y_i\), calibration can be summarized with Brier score:

\[ BS=\frac1n\sum_i(p_i-y_i)^2. \]

Inspect reliability by rule, language, repository class, and scanner version. A globally calibrated 0.8 can hide one rule at 0.98 and another at 0.30. Use temporal holdouts because rule tuning after analyst feedback leaks across random splits. Enforce a hard cutoff: develop on evidence available through time (T), then validate only on predictions emitted after (T). Future developer reactions, fixes, and post-hoc refactors must not be joined back into the training side of that boundary.

Persist the raw candidate population at inference time, before suppression, deduplication, severity guards, or posting policy. Evaluate detector quality and calibration on the eligible raw population, with disposition as an explicit field; evaluate developer burden on the posted subset. Without this split-collection pattern, downstream filters create selection bias that can make precision appear better while hiding discarded candidates.

Finding-level precision also rewards ten correct symptoms of one defect. Group findings by a shared fix boundary—library version, missing authorization policy, sanitizer defect, or generated template—and report unique confirmed root causes, fragmentation, over-merging, review minutes, and tickets created. Exact file-line matching fails after refactoring; text similarity over-merges generic messages. Candidate keys should include CWE, repository lineage, sink API, sanitizer state, trace structure, dependency identity, and fix boundary.

At review budget \(B\), measure distinct root causes discovered per analyst-hour and downstream harm avoided. Do not add these into a universal “quality score”; publish a scorecard so a product cannot trade catastrophic over-merging for a small precision gain.

Safe Lab: Quality Scorecard

rows = [
 # id, confidence, outcome, root cause, evidence fields present, review minutes
 ("F1", .90, 1, "R1", 5, 8),
 ("F2", .80, 1, "R1", 4, 6), # duplicate symptom
 ("F3", .70, 0, None, 2, 12),
 ("F4", .60, 1, "R2", 5, 15),
 ("F5", .40, 0, None, 3, 5),
 ("F6", .55, None, None, 1, 20), # inconclusive
]
labeled = [r for r in rows if r[2] is not None]
roots = {r[3] for r in labeled if r[2] == 1}
scorecard = {
 "reviewed_precision": round(sum(r[2] for r in labeled) / len(labeled), 3),
 "brier": round(sum((r[1]-r[2])**2 for r in labeled) / len(labeled), 3),
 "evidence_completeness": round(sum(r[4]/5 for r in rows) / len(rows), 3),
 "confirmed_findings": sum(r[2] == 1 for r in labeled),
 "distinct_root_causes": len(roots),
 "review_minutes_per_root_cause": round(sum(r[5] for r in rows)/len(roots), 1),
 "inconclusive_rate": round(sum(r[2] is None for r in rows)/len(rows), 3),
}
expected = {'reviewed_precision': .6, 'brier': .172,
 'evidence_completeness': .667, 'confirmed_findings': 3,
 'distinct_root_causes': 2, 'review_minutes_per_root_cause': 33.0,
 'inconclusive_rate': .167}
assert scorecard == expected, scorecard
print(scorecard)

Three confirmed findings represent two root causes. Optimizing confirmed-findings rewards F2; a customer-oriented metric recognizes its smaller incremental value.

Gold Sets, Challenges, and Production Failure

A gold set should combine seeded weaknesses, historical confirmed cases frozen before rule development, clean controls, and independently found production cases. Keep a locked temporal holdout, remove training clones, and report each stratum separately. Challenge sets target path explosion, framework magic, conditional sanitizers, generated code, polyglot boundaries, unreachable utilities, renamed APIs, and adversarial comments containing vulnerability vocabulary.

Inter-reviewer disagreement is information. Cohen’s kappa can flag an underspecified rubric, but consensus must not erase original judgments. Reviewers should be blinded to model confidence on a sample. Developer dismissal is not ground truth: it can mean false positive, accepted risk, duplicate, missing ownership, or deadline pressure.

Calibrate reviewers before promoting a gold set:

  1. select a representative calibration set, often 30–50 findings across important strata;
  2. have qualified reviewers label it independently and blindly;
  3. compute raw agreement plus a chance-corrected measure appropriate to the labels;
  4. for weak or systematically confused categories, adjudicate examples, revise the written rubric, and repeat on a fresh calibration set.

Do not turn a threshold such as κ ≥ 0.70 into a universal law. Predeclare it for the decision, report prevalence and category-specific disagreement, and retain the original labels so a high aggregate agreement score cannot conceal failure on rare critical classes.

Major production failures include:

  • Verification bias: analysts review high scores first. Randomly sample below threshold or weight by review propensity.
  • Mutable truth: reconstruct the emitted commit and lockfile; a finding fixed before review is not detector error.
  • Aggregate hiding: require rule-level intervals and quarantine harmful rules even when global precision rises.
  • Severity inflation: confirmation proves existence, not exploitability or impact.
  • Benchmark overfitting: once a vendor tunes on an evaluation set, retire it to training history and create a new holdout.
  • Duplicate gaming: count both finding and root-cause outcomes, plus over-merge and fragmentation harm.

Operate scorecards by scanner version. Monitor evidence completeness, environment blocks, confirmation, inconclusive outcomes, calibration, root-cause yield, duplicate burden, and validation time. Release gates must name acceptable regressions; “overall score improved” is insufficient.

Constructing a Defensible Evaluation Program

The evaluation population should match the product claim. A scanner marketed for pull-request prevention must be tested on changes as they appeared at review time, not only on mature repositories after fixes and refactors. A cloud posture product needs tenants with different providers, policy maturity, and asset scale. A binary analyzer needs compiler, architecture, and optimization diversity. Write the claim first—population, artifact, weakness families, latency, and intended action—then sample.

Sampling is part of the estimator. If every critical finding is reviewed, 10% of highs, and 1% of mediums, raw confirmed proportions cannot be added. Record the inclusion probability and use inverse-probability weighting for population estimates. Publish unweighted counts alongside weighted rates so readers can see support. Extremely large weights produce unstable estimates; combine strata or increase sampling rather than hiding the variance.

Confidence intervals matter most where sample sizes are small. A new rule with four confirmations in four reviews does not have proven 100% precision. Use a binomial interval or Bayesian posterior with a declared prior, and require minimum evidence before autonomous suppression or blocking. For calibration bins, report count and uncertainty. Empty regions of the confidence scale reveal that the model’s numeric precision is cosmetic.

Reproducibility protocol

A reproducibility package should pin the artifact, build configuration, runtime, request or input fixture, relevant identity, expected observation, and cleanup. Secrets must be synthetic or ephemeral. The package must not exploit production systems. For code findings, include the shortest trace demonstrating source, transformations, guards, and sink. For cloud findings, include read-only configuration evidence and a safe policy evaluation. For endpoint findings, prefer captured telemetry or a disposable virtual machine.

Reproduction can produce several outcomes: mechanism confirmed; claim refuted; trigger blocked by environment; evidence insufficient; or artifact no longer available. These outcomes guide different improvements. A high environment-block rate suggests the product emits claims customers cannot validate. A high unavailable-artifact rate suggests retention or commit-resolution defects. Folding both into “inconclusive” loses engineering direction.

Time to validate is not merely an operations metric. It is a property of finding design. Compare otherwise similar findings with and without traces, concrete inputs, ownership hints, and fix boundaries. A controlled evaluation can randomize evidence presentation to reviewers and measure validation time and correct disposition. Do not expose a potentially misleading model confidence in the treatment unless the experiment is specifically testing confidence display.

Severity, exploitability, and actionability

Severity describes consequence under conditions; exploitability describes how feasible those conditions are; business impact describes what the affected system matters to the organization. Keep these as fields. A path traversal in a build tool may have high technical impact but require trusted local access; an authorization bypass in a low-CVSS internal service may expose regulated data through a reachable identity path.

Actionability can be scored through observable components: correct owner located, fix boundary identified, remediation available, reproduction fixture present, and estimated effort. It should not be inferred from “ticket closed.” Teams sometimes close excellent findings because risk is accepted and retain poor findings because audit policy requires them. Measure evidence quality before downstream organizational choices.

Root-cause labeling also needs a contract. Two findings share a root cause when one bounded change can remove the relevant mechanism without separately addressing each symptom. This definition is deliberately tied to remediation. The same CWE in two independently maintained libraries is not one root cause. Conversely, different CWE symptoms may share one unsafe code-generation template. Store the proposed cluster, algorithm version, reviewer decision, and final fix identifier.

Metamorphic and adversarial tests

Known-answer benchmarks test cases, but metamorphic tests examine invariants. Rename variables, reorder independent statements, move code without changing data flow, or replace a sanitizer with an equivalent wrapper. A robust semantic analyzer should preserve its conclusion. Then alter the actual security property—remove authorization, change the sanitizer context, or make a path attacker-controlled—and require the conclusion to change.

Adversarial cases should target the product surface, not merely the model. Put vulnerability words in comments, create very long traces, use generated filenames resembling dependencies, produce conflicting package manifests, and inject malformed source maps. Test whether parsers fail closed, fail open, or silently assign a default severity. A safe product exposes unsupported analysis rather than fabricating confidence.

Release and rollback

Before release, replay the candidate on a fixed corpus and a recent production sample. Compare paired outcomes: new confirmed root causes, lost root causes, confidence changes, duplicate clusters, evidence regressions, and latency. Aggregate lift cannot justify losing coverage for a dangerous weakness family. Establish must-not-regress challenge cases and maximum queue expansion by customer segment.

Canary the scanner version on consenting repositories. Keep old and new finding identities linked so users do not receive duplicate tickets during migration. If rollback occurs, restore compatible suppression, cluster, and confidence semantics. Merely reverting the engine while leaving new identifiers in workflow systems can reopen thousands of items.

Quality governance should separate product targets from adjudication rules. The team rewarded for precision must not decide after seeing results whether duplicates count as true positives. Version the rubric before evaluation, log exceptions, and have an independent review for high-impact automated actions such as merge blocking. This turns the scorecard into evidence rather than marketing.

Reading a Scorecard as an Engineering Decision

Suppose a candidate release raises reviewed precision from 78% to 84%, reduces median validation time from 18 to 11 minutes, but loses 9 of 40 authentication-bypass cases in the locked challenge set. The release is not “better” in the only sense that matters. The regression affects a high-consequence family and may reflect a parser or framework-modeling change. Block general rollout, isolate the responsible rule path, and consider shipping unaffected languages behind separate version flags.

Now suppose the lost cases are duplicate symptoms already represented by another finding. The answer changes only if the duplicate analysis is independently validated and the surviving finding reaches the same owner with equal evidence. A finding suppressed because two traces look similar is not safely redundant when the traces cross different trust boundaries or require different fixes. Review over-merge errors at the actual automation boundary.

Scorecards should include denominators and abstentions. If a scanner analyzes 70% of files and achieves 90% precision there, it must not be compared directly with a scanner analyzing 98% at 82% precision. Report unsupported files, parser failures, timeouts, and intentionally skipped generated code. Coverage-weighted yield can help, but keep the components visible because customers may care disproportionately about the unsupported 2%.

Performance also has a quality dimension. A pull-request scanner that returns excellent findings after forty minutes may arrive after merge. Measure end-to-end decision latency at realistic repository sizes and concurrent load, including cache misses. Timeout behavior must be explicit: allow, block, retry, or fall back. Silent partial results make precision estimates meaningless because the evaluated population changes with system load.

For generative remediation, evaluate the patch separately from the finding. A correct diagnosis can yield an insecure or behavior-breaking patch. Run tests, static checks, policy checks, and targeted security fixtures in an isolated environment. Measure patch acceptance, modifications by developers, introduced defects, and whether the root cause remains. Never let an accepted generated patch retroactively validate the original finding; developers may accept changes for unrelated reasons.

Cross-customer comparison demands care. Different customers configure rules, suppressions, and severity policies; their reviewed populations and incentives differ. Normalize only within a declared configuration and sampling design. A benchmark percentile that mixes permissive advisory deployments with strict merge-blocking deployments is uninterpretable. Product analytics should help each customer understand its own evidence quality without leaking another tenant’s code or labels.

The final review artifact should include the claim being tested, corpus manifest, sampling probabilities, reviewer rubric, disagreement record, scanner artifacts, result tables with uncertainty, known benchmark overlap, and a signed decision. Reproducibility here means another authorized team can recreate the evaluation from retained, access-controlled artifacts—not that vulnerable customer code is broadly copied.

Sources and Further Reading

  • NIST Software Assurance Reference Dataset. Controlled known-good and known-bad programs, with limited external validity. https://samate.nist.gov/SARD/
  • OWASP Benchmark Project. A repeatable Java test suite that should be one evaluation stratum, not the sole production claim. https://owasp.org/www-project-benchmark/
  • MITRE CWE. Shared weakness vocabulary; identical CWE identifiers do not prove a common root cause. https://cwe.mitre.org/
  • ISO/IEC 29147:2018. Coordinated receipt, verification, and communication expectations for vulnerability disclosure. https://www.iso.org/standard/72311.html
  • NIST SP 800-218. Connects vulnerability response to secure development and durable process improvement. https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/218/final

Benchmarks supply known cases, CWE supplies vocabulary, and standards supply workflow expectations. Finding quality still requires reproducibility, calibrated confidence, root-cause novelty, and human cost.

Interview Practicum

Scenario: The Denominator Changes.

Prompt. A new SAST engine reports 92% precision on 500 reviewed findings versus 71% for the incumbent. Should the company migrate?

Ask how samples were selected, whether reviewers were blinded, how inconclusive cases were handled, whether commits were frozen, what languages were covered, and whether duplicates count.

Worked Answer

Replay both tools on identical repositories, adjudicate stratified random samples including low scores, group root causes, and compare results at the same review budget.

Follow-Up Questions and Answers

Change one: the 500 new-engine findings were its top-ranked outputs; the incumbent sample was uniform. The headline comparison is invalid. Uniformly sample both or use inclusion-probability weights. A top-of-list evaluation may answer a capacity question, but then compare unique root causes per analyst-hour.

Change two: migration removes the incumbent’s binary-analysis coverage for 20% of releases. Evaluate a portfolio. Retain the incumbent for uncovered artifacts until an alternative passes a challenge set, and deduplicate cross-tool output. Coverage loss is harm, not a precision footnote.
