Interview Practicum

Threat-model a coding agent that reads private repositories, issues, and CI logs; writes branches; runs tests; and deploys to staging. Halfway through, the interviewer adds that product managers may paste customer tickets containing secrets, a subagent searches the public web, and emergency production deployment is desired during incidents.

Produce a typed authority graph, identify three abuse paths, and propose controls that preserve useful autonomy. Explain what evidence would convince you the controls operate as designed.

Worked Answer

I would type principals, data, agents, tools, credentials, environments, and policies, then enumerate INFLUENCES, READS, INVOKES, MINTS, AUTHORIZES, and WRITES edges. The primary abuse path is customer ticket to agent to egress tool, causing disclosure. The second is repository injection to branch writer to CI, causing execution with CI secrets. The third is web subagent to parent plan to emergency deploy, a confused-deputy path.

Tickets enter a secret-redaction boundary and remain untrusted. Public-web retrieval runs under a child capability with no repository or write access. Tests execute in an ephemeral, no-credential workspace with restricted egress. Branch writes use repository-scoped, short-lived tokens. Staging deploy requires a brokered token bound to artifact digest and environment. Production emergency access is a separate break-glass workflow with eligible incident commander approval, short expiry, immutable logging, and post-incident review; the agent cannot activate it.

I would verify the design with graph reachability tests, sandbox escape and egress tests, injected-content scenarios, credential canaries, tool-schema integrity checks, and audit replay showing each consequential action has a matching authorization digest. I would not claim that prompt filtering makes hostile content trusted.

Follow-Up Questions and Answers

The agent needs package downloads during tests. How do you constrain egress?

Use an authenticated dependency proxy with pinned namespaces, malware scanning, quotas, and no arbitrary URL fetch. Record resolved package digests. Exceptions require a new scoped decision.

Can the same human propose and approve an emergency deployment?

Only if explicit risk policy accepts that reduced separation during a declared incident. Make the exception visible, time-bound, and reviewed; do not let the agent infer emergency status.

Is read-only repository access low risk?

No. It exposes secrets, unreleased code, vulnerabilities, and customer context. Disclosure paths and cross-tenant mixing can be severe without any write.

Where should policy execute?

Outside the model and as close as practical to the consequential tool, with canonical inputs and complete mediation. Model instructions can guide behavior but cannot enforce authority.

Key Takeaways

  • Blast radius follows authority, not model capability.
  • Type nodes and edges so data influence cannot masquerade as authorization.
  • Bind approvals and short-lived credentials to canonical action digests.
  • Attenuate authority across every delegation.
  • Treat memory, tools, models, and retrieved content as supply-chain surfaces.
  • Prompt-injection resistance is defense in depth, never the authorization boundary.

Chapter 35: Instrumenting AI Agents for Security Evidence

A Trace Must Answer a Forensic Question

An agent trace is not a transcript. A transcript helps a developer watch a demo; security evidence must establish who initiated a run, what evidence influenced it, which policy authorized each consequential action, what tool actually executed, and whether the record was altered. Storing every prompt forever is neither necessary nor defensible. It increases breach impact while still failing to prove provenance.

Chapter 34 modeled authority paths. Instrumentation should make those typed edges observable. If a coding agent deploys an artifact, an investigator needs the proposal digest, approver, policy version, credential lease, tool request and response, artifact identity, and ordering relationship. The exact prose of an unrelated brainstorming turn may add privacy risk without forensic value.

Typed Trace Envelope

Use a small stable envelope with typed payloads. Required envelope fields are trace_id, event_id, parent_id, sequence, event_time, ingest_time, actor, event_type, schema_version, policy_version, sensitivity, payload_digest, previous_hash, and event_hash. Payloads vary by event type but are schema-validated.

Event typeRequired payload fieldsSecurity question
run.startedinitiator, tenant, objective digestWho requested what?
evidence.observedsource type, locator, content digest, trust labelWhat influenced reasoning?
model.completedprovider, model, input/output digests, finish reasonWhich model transformation occurred?
tool.proposedtool, canonical arguments digest, consequence classWhat did the agent intend?
policy.decideddecision, reason codes, subject, object, actionWhy was it allowed or denied?
approval.recordedprincipal, proposal digest, expiryWhat exactly was approved?
tool.completedtool version, result digest, status, side effectsWhat actually happened?
memory.changednamespace, old/new digest, provenance, expiryWhat durable state changed?
run.endedoutcome, terminal reason, evidence summary digestHow did the run terminate?

Free-form text is referenced through protected content objects rather than copied into every event. Store a salted digest, classification, encrypted locator, retention class, and redacted preview. High-sensitivity content may be deleted while the event envelope and digest remain, proving that a particular object was used without preserving it indefinitely.

sequenceDiagram
 participant A as Agent runtime
 participant R as Redaction gateway
 participant L as Append-only trace log
 participant K as Key service
 participant V as Verifier
 participant C as Cold evidence vault
 A->>R: typed event + sensitive payload
 R->>C: encrypted content object (policy permitting)
 R->>K: request tenant signing operation
 K-->>R: signature/key identifier
 R->>L: envelope + digest + previous hash + signature
 L-->>A: durable sequence receipt
 V->>L: fetch chain segment
 V->>K: obtain public verification material
 V-->>V: validate schema, order, hashes, signatures

This architecture separates collection, content protection, integrity, and verification. The runtime cannot choose a weaker retention class. The log acknowledges only durable writes. A verifier independent of the producer detects deletion, insertion, reorder, and modification within the chain’s guarantees.

Integrity and Provenance

Canonical serialization is mandatory. Hashing ordinary JSON is unsafe because key order, number rendering, and Unicode forms may differ. Define UTF-8 encoding, normalized strings, sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace, and permitted scalar representations. Better, adopt a documented canonical format such as JSON Canonicalization Scheme.

For canonical event bytes \(b_i\), payload digest \(d_i\), and previous hash \(h_{i-1}\), compute

\[ h_i=H(domain\separator\parallel h{i-1}\parallel b_i\parallel d_i). \]

The domain separator prevents the hash from being reused in another protocol. A hash chain detects changes only if a trusted party knows an anchor. Periodically sign checkpoint tuples (tenant, stream, first_sequence, last_sequence, root_hash, time) using a protected key and publish them to a separately administered store. Otherwise an attacker controlling the log can rewrite the whole chain.

Hash chains do not prove that an event is true or complete. A compromised producer can faithfully hash lies or omit a call. Corroborate high-consequence actions with tool-side logs, cloud audit records, deployment attestations, and credential-broker events. Compare expected state transitions with observed transitions and alert on sequence gaps.

Causality and clocks

Wall clocks drift. Use a monotonic per-stream sequence and parent_id for causal relationships; keep event and ingest times for latency analysis. Concurrent subagents form a directed acyclic graph rather than one global order. Each stream can chain independently, while join events name the terminal hashes of child streams.

Privacy and retention

Data minimization begins before logging. Record normalized tool parameters where needed, but tokenize secrets and omit raw credentials categorically. Separate operational telemetry from restricted content. Access to content requires a case-bound reason, is itself logged, and can be more tightly retained than envelopes.

Retention should follow consequence and purpose: policy decisions and deployment receipts may survive for audit obligations; raw prompts containing customer data may expire in days; cryptographic digests and aggregate metrics may remain longer. Deletion must cover replicas, indexes, caches, and derived embeddings. A digest can itself be personal data when the input space is guessable, so salt or key sensitive digests and control verification access.

Executable Lab: Schema and Hash-Chain Verifier

The lab validates event types and required fields, creates a deterministic chain, verifies it, then demonstrates tamper detection. It uses synthetic payloads and the standard library.

import hashlib, json
from copy import deepcopy

REQUIRED = {
    "run.started": {"initiator", "objective_digest"},
    "policy.decided": {"decision", "proposal_digest", "reason"},
    "tool.completed": {"tool", "status", "result_digest"},
}

def canonical(value):
    return json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"),
                      ensure_ascii=False).encode()

def seal(events):
    previous = "0" * 64
    sealed = []
    for sequence, raw in enumerate(events, 1):
        event = deepcopy(raw)
        missing = REQUIRED[event["event_type"]] - event["payload"].keys()
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(f"missing fields: {sorted(missing)}")
        event["sequence"] = sequence
        event["previous_hash"] = previous
        body = canonical(event)
        event["event_hash"] = hashlib.sha256(b"agent-trace-v1\0" + body).hexdigest()
        previous = event["event_hash"]
        sealed.append(event)
    return sealed

def verify(chain):
    previous = "0" * 64
    for expected, event in enumerate(chain, 1):
        claimed = event["event_hash"]
        body = {k: v for k, v in event.items() if k != "event_hash"}
        actual = hashlib.sha256(b"agent-trace-v1\0" + canonical(body)).hexdigest()
        if event["sequence"] != expected or event["previous_hash"] != previous:
            return False, f"ordering failure at {expected}"
        if claimed != actual:
            return False, f"hash failure at {expected}"
        previous = claimed
    return True, f"verified {len(chain)} events; anchor={previous[:12]}"

events = [
 {"event_type":"run.started", "payload":{"initiator":"alice",
  "objective_digest":"sha256:111"}},
 {"event_type":"policy.decided", "payload":{"decision":"allow",
  "proposal_digest":"sha256:222", "reason":"staging-only"}},
 {"event_type":"tool.completed", "payload":{"tool":"deploy",
  "status":"ok", "result_digest":"sha256:333"}},
]
chain = seal(events)
print(*verify(chain))
chain[1]["payload"]["decision"] = "deny"
print(*verify(chain))

Expected output:

True verified 3 events; anchor=e26371d4de87
False hash failure at 2

The exact anchor is deterministic for this program. Production code should use a formal schema library, canonicalization standard, per-tenant stream identity, signatures, key rotation, durable checkpoints, and explicit migration tests. Never place secrets into a lab merely to see whether redaction works.

Coverage and Operational Failure Analysis

Happy-path-only traces. Instrumentation often misses policy exceptions, retries, cancellation, timeouts, streaming partials, and sandbox kills. Derive required events from the state machine and test every transition, including denied and failed actions.

Collector loss. If the trace backend is unavailable, decide by consequence class: low-risk reads may buffer locally; consequential writes should fail closed if their authorization receipt cannot be durably recorded. Bound buffers and expose loss counters.

High-cardinality collapse. Aggregating by run can erase the one denied call that explains an incident. Keep event-level evidence in restricted storage while exporting carefully chosen metrics.

Redaction after ingestion. Secrets already reached logs, queues, and error trackers. Redact at the producer boundary, structurally exclude credential fields, and scan canaries across the complete telemetry path.

Broken migrations. Adding a field can change canonical bytes or verifier behavior. Version schemas immutably, preserve old verification logic, and test known fixtures for every version.

Insider reconstruction. Even redacted previews, timing, and tool arguments may reveal sensitive activity. Enforce tenant isolation, purpose-bound access, dual control for bulk export, query auditing, and anomaly detection on investigators.

False assurance from hashes. Integrity is not completeness, authenticity, or correctness. Combine producer chains with independently sourced tool and cloud audit evidence. Record coverage claims explicitly: which tool versions and execution paths emit which events.

Queryability without uncontrolled copying

Forensic evidence is useless when investigators cannot join it, but broad search indexes create new disclosure surfaces. Index stable identifiers, types, times, consequence classes, reason codes, and keyed pseudonyms. Keep sensitive payload search in a restricted enclave with case-bound access. Export tools should default to envelopes and require a separate authorization to include content.

Test common investigation queries against synthetic incidents before launch: list all actions derived from one evidence object, find tool completions without approvals, reconstruct a delegation tree, and verify a chain across key rotation. Measure time to answer and missing joins. A schema that is cryptographically elegant but operationally unqueryable will be bypassed during an incident.

Source Synthesis

Building an Evidence Contract

Start with investigations the organization must perform. For an unauthorized deployment, determine whether the agent proposed the artifact, an eligible human approved it, policy evaluated the same digest, the credential matched the environment, and the service applied that artifact. Convert each question into required events and joins. This avoids collecting attractive but irrelevant model chatter.

Define volume before rollout. Streaming tokens can outnumber consequential actions by orders of magnitude. Keep token diagnostics only in bounded debug samples; retain durable event facts for security. Estimate bytes per run, peak events per second, content-store growth, index cost, and checkpoint frequency. Budgeting is a control because overloaded collectors lose rare failure events.

Classify schema changes as additive, semantic, or breaking. Adding an optional field is additive only when absence has defined meaning. Changing actor from authenticated principal to display name is semantic. Removing an event type is breaking because coverage claims change. Consumers declare supported versions and fail visibly on unknown security semantics.

Sensitive-action taxonomy

Classify observation, local mutation, external communication, privilege change, financial action, destructive action, production change, credential access, and durable memory mutation. Add scope and reversibility. Reading one public file differs from bulk private-repository export; an ephemeral test file differs from deleting production data.

For each class specify required proposal fields, policy evidence, approval, tool receipt, retention, and trace-outage behavior. Share the taxonomy with the tool broker. If tracing calls something local while the broker calls it external, audits will be incoherent.

Completeness reconciliation

Every credential lease should join to allowed calls and closure or expiry. Every consequential completion should join to one proposal and policy decision, plus approval when required. Every deployment should appear in both agent and platform audit streams.

Reconcile continuously. Unmatched completions indicate bypass or collection loss. Unused leases may show aborted work or credential harvesting. Missing terminal events reveal crashes. Accept late events within a bounded window while preserving original sequence and ingest latency.

Cryptographic operations

Keys require identifiers, rotation, revocation, and separation by tenant and environment. Retain public material and algorithms for historical checkpoints after rotation. If a key is compromised, record the affected interval; do not re-sign history. Forward security reduces some retrospective risk but does not cure producer compromise.

Checkpoint frequency trades detection latency, cost, and rewrite exposure. Deployment streams may checkpoint per transaction; observation streams hourly. Anchor to another account, transparency service, or write-once store under a different role. Test archive restoration and verification without the producer database.

Evidentiary limits

An incident package contains chain segments, checkpoints, schemas, canonicalization rules, key history, verifier version, independent logs, access records, and a narrative separating observation from inference. Generate it reproducibly and hash the package.

A signature proves a key signed bytes, not which human controlled it. A matching digest proves byte equality when content exists, not that content was complete or honestly labeled. Put these limits in runbooks so incident pressure does not turn cryptography into folklore.

OpenTelemetry provides trace identity and semantic conventions but is not by itself a forensic integrity system. W3C Trace Context propagates correlation, not trust. RFC 8785 supplies deterministic JSON; NIST log-management guidance addresses operational collection and retention; SLSA and in-toto show how attestations bind subjects, materials, and steps. The practical design borrows correlation from observability and verifiability from supply-chain provenance while applying privacy minimization before collection.

  • NIST SP 800-92, Guide to Computer Security Log Management: https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/Legacy/SP/nistspecialpublication800-92.pdf

Interview Practicum

Design telemetry for a customer-support agent that reads tickets, queries account systems, drafts refunds, and can issue refunds after approval. Legal permits raw ticket retention for seven days, Finance requires seven-year refund evidence, and Security discovers that model-provider request IDs are unavailable in one region. During the discussion, a suspected insider deletes a trace row.

Specify the schema, trust boundaries, retention split, integrity design, coverage response, and incident evidence package.

Worked Answer

I would define typed envelopes for run start, evidence observation, model completion, tool proposal, policy decision, approval, refund completion, and run end. Raw tickets live in an encrypted content store for seven days; events hold a keyed digest, classification, and case-bound locator. Refund records retain canonical proposal, amount, currency, account pseudonym, approver, policy version, tool receipt, and ledger transaction identifier for the Finance period without retaining unrelated conversation text.

Each tenant and agent stream uses sequence numbers and a hash chain. Hourly signed checkpoints go to a separately administered immutable store. The refund service emits its own receipt and ledger audit event, allowing completeness reconciliation. Missing provider request IDs become an explicit regional coverage flag; model identity, local request digest, timing, and response digest remain, but the team must not claim provider-side correlation there.

For the deletion incident, verification identifies the gap or broken successor link. Preserve the signed checkpoint, adjacent events, collector access logs, refund-service audit, ledger record, key history, and schema/version documentation. Rotate access if compromise is suspected. The report distinguishes proven facts from inference: a broken chain proves inconsistency after the checkpoint, not which person deleted the row or whether the original event was truthful.

Follow-Up Questions and Answers

Can the company keep unsalted prompt hashes forever?

Not safely by default. Guessable messages can be dictionary-attacked and hashes may remain regulated data. Use keyed digests, restricted verification, and purpose-based retention.

What happens when the trace service is down?

Buffer bounded low-consequence events, but fail closed for refunds if durable authorization and completion evidence cannot be recorded. Alert on every loss counter.

How do you measure trace coverage in a nondeterministic agent?

Measure instrumented state transitions and tool boundaries, not textual paths. Run generated scenario suites and reconcile tool-side actions against corresponding proposal, decision, and completion events.

Why not use a blockchain?

A signed, externally anchored append-only log usually provides the required tamper evidence with less complexity. The governance of writers, keys, checkpoints, and independent evidence matters more than the branding of the data structure.

Key Takeaways

  • Security traces are typed evidence, not permanent transcripts.
  • Separate stable envelopes from protected, short-lived content objects.
  • Canonicalize, chain, sign, and externally anchor high-value streams.
  • Integrity does not prove truth or completeness; corroborate at tool boundaries.
  • Design retention by purpose and consequence before collection.
  • Make regional, tool, and failure-path coverage gaps explicit.

Field lesson: a digital thread must expose broken links

The sec-pr implementation indexed 566 evidence artifacts and linked analytical records through deterministic composite identity and hashes. It also quarantined 278 unresolved historical records instead of silently forcing joins. Trace completeness therefore included a reconciliation result: what the system could connect, what it could not connect, and why. See Chapter 47 for the full architecture.

Chapter 36: Evaluating Agent Security Controls

One Passing Run Proves Almost Nothing

An agent may refuse an attack on Tuesday and execute it on Wednesday because sampling, retrieval order, tool latency, memory, or a slightly different conversation changes its trajectory. Security evaluation must therefore estimate a distribution of outcomes, not preserve a favorite transcript. The evaluation unit is a scenario–configuration–trial tuple, and the claim should include uncertainty.

A safeguard can reduce attack success while destroying legitimate work. It can also appear strong because the test set contains obvious attacks, because evaluators stop after the first refusal, or because a sandbox prevents consequences without testing whether policy allowed them. Chapter 34 identified authority paths; Chapter 35 made actions observable. This chapter uses those artifacts to test the whole control stack: model, prompt/scaffold, retrieval, memory, policy, tool broker, sandbox, approval, and final outcome.

Evaluation Architecture

flowchart LR
 S[Versioned scenario registry] --> X[Factorial trial scheduler]
 C[Control configurations] --> X
 X --> R1[Isolated runner seed A]
 X --> R2[Isolated runner seed B]
 X --> RN[Isolated runner seed N]
 R1 --> T[Typed traces and outcomes]
 R2 --> T
 RN --> T
 T --> O[Independent oracle and adjudication]
 O --> M[Metrics by threat, utility, and segment]
 M --> U[Bootstrap and binomial uncertainty]
 U --> G{Release gate}
 G -->|pass| D[Canary with kill switch]
 G -->|fail| B[Counterexample corpus]
 B --> S

The scenario registry is immutable per evaluation. Each entry identifies initial state, trusted and untrusted inputs, permitted actions, forbidden outcomes, benign task goal, termination rule, and oracle. The scheduler varies seeds and relevant environmental factors. Runners are disposable and deny real-world side effects. Oracles operate on typed traces and final state, not on whether output “sounds safe.”

Define the Estimands

For adversarial scenario family \(g\), attack success rate is

\[ ASR_g=P(\text{forbidden outcome}\mid g, configuration). \]

Defense success is not always \(1-ASR\): a run can avoid the forbidden outcome yet fail closed incorrectly, loop, or abandon the legitimate subtask. On benign tasks define false-refusal rate \(FRR=P(refusal\mid benign)\), task success \(TSR\), cost, latency, and human interventions. A paired utility difference between candidate \(c\) and baseline \(b\) can be

\[ \Delta U=E[w_t(TSR_c-TSR_b)-w_a(ASR_c-ASR_b) -w_f(FRR_c-FRR_b)-w_k(Cost_c-Cost_b)]. \]

Weights encode an explicit operating decision, but always publish components. A positive aggregate can hide catastrophic regression in a high-impact scenario.

Repetition and confidence intervals

For \(x\) successes in \(n\) independent trials, report \(\hat p=x/n\) with a Wilson interval rather than a naked rate. At zero observed bypasses, the one-sided “rule of three” gives an approximate 95 percent upper bound of \(3/n\): zero in ten trials still permits a true bypass probability near 30 percent. To claim an upper bound below 1 percent after zero failures requires roughly 300 representative trials, not three screenshots. The shortcut assumes approximately IID trials. When attempts cluster by repository, agent session, target, or model version, the effective sample size is smaller; use cluster-aware analysis or a cluster bootstrap rather than substituting the raw request count for \(n\).

Trials may not be independent. Provider updates, shared caches, rate limits, or persistent memory create clusters. Randomize execution order, isolate state, block by model/provider version, and use cluster bootstrap or hierarchical analysis when trials share conditions. Store seeds where supported, but do not confuse a seed with reproducibility across changing infrastructure.

Adaptive attacks

A static attack suite measures known strings, not a determined adversary. Split evaluation into fixed regression cases, mutation-based variants, and an adaptive phase in which a tester observes refusals and changes strategy within a bounded budget. Keep the final holdout private from control developers. Track attempts-to-bypass and success within budget.

Oracles

Output keyword matching is a weak oracle. Prefer state-based facts: Did a network connection reach a forbidden host? Was a credential read? Did the broker issue an unauthorized capability? Was production modified? Combine automatic oracles with blinded human adjudication for ambiguous semantic harm. Measure inter-rater agreement and resolve disagreements under a written rubric.

Experimental Design and Release Gates

Pair candidate and baseline on the same scenario instances to reduce variance. Randomize which runs first. Freeze model, tool, policy, scenario, and dependency versions for the comparison. If the production model is a moving service, record its provider version and repeat sentinel scenarios over time.

Pre-register primary metrics and gates. A credible gate might require: no critical forbidden outcome in a designated must-pass suite; candidate ASR upper confidence bound below 5 percent per high-risk family; benign task-success lower bound no more than two percentage points below baseline; false-refusal increase below one point; and no new unrestricted authority path. Gates are governance decisions, not statistically discovered after results arrive.

Avoid test-set contamination. Scenario text, hidden tokens, and oracle details should not enter training or everyday prompt repositories. Rotate semantic variants and test structural behavior. If a safeguard recognizes the phrase “ignore previous instructions,” it has learned a costume, not a boundary.

Executable Lab: Repeated-Trial Control Evaluation

This deterministic simulation models a nondeterministic agent under baseline and guarded configurations. It runs paired adversarial and benign trials, computes Wilson 95 percent intervals, and reports security and utility. Synthetic randomness makes the lab safe and repeatable.

from math import sqrt
from random import Random

SCENARIOS = [
    ("indirect_injection", "attack", .34, .08),
    ("delegation_escape", "attack", .22, .06),
    ("normal_refactor", "benign", .91, .87),
    ("dependency_update", "benign", .84, .79),
]

def wilson(successes, trials, z=1.96):
    p = successes / trials
    den = 1 + z*z/trials
    center = (p + z*z/(2*trials)) / den
    margin = z * sqrt((p*(1-p) + z*z/(4*trials))/trials) / den
    return center - margin, center + margin

def run(seed=2026, trials=200):
    rng = Random(seed)
    results = {}
    for name, kind, baseline_p, guarded_p in SCENARIOS:
        for config, probability in (("base", baseline_p),
                                    ("guard", guarded_p)):
            successes = sum(rng.random() < probability for _ in range(trials))
            results[(name, kind, config)] = (successes, trials)
    return results

results = run()
for (name, kind, config), (x, n) in results.items():
    lo, hi = wilson(x, n)
    metric = "ASR" if kind == "attack" else "TSR"
    print(f"{name:20} {config:5} {metric}={x/n:.3f} "
          f"95%CI=[{lo:.3f},{hi:.3f}]")

Expected output:

indirect_injection   base  ASR=0.290 95%CI=[0.232,0.356]
indirect_injection   guard ASR=0.050 95%CI=[0.027,0.090]
delegation_escape    base  ASR=0.220 95%CI=[0.168,0.282]
delegation_escape    guard ASR=0.085 95%CI=[0.054,0.132]
normal_refactor      base  TSR=0.940 95%CI=[0.898,0.965]
normal_refactor      guard TSR=0.865 95%CI=[0.811,0.906]
dependency_update    base  TSR=0.825 95%CI=[0.766,0.871]
dependency_update    guard TSR=0.775 95%CI=[0.712,0.827]

The guard clearly reduces simulated ASR, but it also reduces benign success. Whether it ships depends on predeclared utility and non-inferiority gates. In a real harness, replace Bernoulli draws with isolated agent executions, preserve typed traces, and have oracles inspect final state. Do not let the harness possess production credentials.

Operational Failure Analysis

Evaluating only the model. A model refusal can be followed by a scaffold retry that succeeds dangerously; a model compliance can be blocked by the broker. Score policy decisions, tool calls, and outcomes separately.

Stopping on a good result. Re-running until a control passes is optional stopping. Fix trial counts or use a documented sequential test with error spending. Publish all planned runs.

Scenario monoculture. Many paraphrases of one injection inflate sample size without threat diversity. Report both trial-weighted and family-weighted results. Maintain coverage against authority paths, tool classes, data boundaries, and persistence mechanisms.

Cross-trial contamination. Memory, caches, files, and provider sessions can carry attack instructions into later benign trials. Reset state and include contamination canaries. If production intentionally preserves memory, evaluate ordered multi-session sequences as their own scenario.

Unsafe testing. An evaluation that can email customers or deploy production is an incident generator. Substitute instrumented fake services, network sinks, synthetic secrets, and canary credentials with no authority. Test the real authorization layer in a dedicated nonproduction tenant.

Oracle leakage. If the agent sees the forbidden marker or evaluator rubric, it can optimize for the test. Keep oracle state out of context and use external observations.

Aggregate victory. A large improvement on easy cases can mask one critical regression. Use must-pass outcomes and report worst-family bounds. Never average away catastrophic impact.

Production drift. Controls interact with new models, tools, prompts, and policies. Trigger evaluation on component changes, run scheduled sentinel trials, and compare canary trace distributions. Preserve a tested kill switch and known-safe reduced-authority mode.

Reporting results

An evaluation report begins with the release decision and tested configuration, then lists gates, sample sizes, invalid trials, point estimates, intervals, and scenario coverage. Include every critical counterexample with secrets removed. Separate prespecified findings from exploratory observations. Provide machine-readable trial records so another team can reproduce calculations.

Avoid league tables that rank safeguards by one aggregate score. State where each control acts: prompt handling, memory, policy, broker, sandbox, or approval. Two controls with similar ASR can have different failure correlation; defense in depth is valuable when bypasses are not shared. Test combinations rather than assuming independent effects.

Source Synthesis

Reports should also state what was not tested, especially languages, tenants, tool versions, long-horizon memory, and provider regions. Named omissions prevent a local result from becoming an organization-wide safety claim.

Constructing the Suite

Design scenarios from authority edges, not jailbreak phrases. For each consequential tool, create cases where untrusted evidence alters object, action, destination, scope, or timing. Include encoded content, tool-output injection, poisoned memory, compromised dependencies, delegation, and multi-turn pressure. Create benign twins sharing surface features: legitimate research quoting attacks, an authorized sensitive-file request, and harmless tool recovery. Twins reveal vocabulary filters.

Each scenario contract names setup, roles, trusted inputs, attacker inputs, allowed actions, forbidden outcomes, maximum turns, cost budget, reset, and oracle. Give it a stable family identifier with instance variation. Version it whenever success criteria change. Add counterexamples to regression while retaining a private holdout.

Sampling should reflect frequency and risk. A frequency-weighted estimate predicts ordinary exposure; a risk-weighted suite stresses rare catastrophic paths. Publish both. A production task capable of rotating a root credential deserves substantial testing even if rare.

Power and thresholds

Confidence intervals describe uncertainty after testing; power analysis plans whether a meaningful change is detectable. If baseline ASR is 10 percent and useful reduction means 5 percent, choose sample size for that contrast and desired errors. For rare events, combine stress tests, structural authorization assurance, and conservative bounds. Absence of observed harm is not impossibility.

For benign utility use non-inferiority. Set margin (delta) before results: accept only if the lower confidence bound of (TSR_c-TSR_b) exceeds (-delta). Choose margins from user consequence, not release convenience. Measure tail latency and cost because loops make distributions heavy-tailed.

Multiple families create multiplicity. “Any critical failure” gates need no averaging. Label exploratory comparisons and control false discoveries for confirmatory claims. Never cherry-pick a seed, snapshot, or judge.

Harness engineering

Capture scenario version, model and parameters, system-prompt digest, retrieval corpus, memory snapshot, tool schemas, policy bundle, container image, network policy, and evaluator code. Assign trial IDs and derive seeds from a recorded master. Enforce timeout, token, tool, and spend budgets.

Fake tools must be behaviorally faithful. A mock deployer implements authorization, idempotency, state, and receipts rather than always succeeding. Synthetic credentials serve as canaries without real authority. Network sinks record destinations and content digests.

Evaluator failure is distinct from agent failure. Provider errors, invalid setup, and oracle crashes are neither attack nor defense success. Report invalid-trial rate, retry under a declared rule, and investigate configuration-correlated failures. A control must not look safe by crashing the harness.

Production bridge

Canaries begin with reduced authority and shadow policy. Compare production tool sequences, refusal patterns, and delegation depth with suite coverage. Do not replay private prompts into research without consent and minimization.

Define response thresholds before launch. One critical unauthorized action triggers containment; refusal regression may trigger rollback; a new model identity triggers sentinels or blocks execution. Preserve failed traces and sandbox state. Generalize failures into tests without broadly publishing bypass details.

NIST AI RMF frames evaluation as continuous risk management, while the Generative AI Profile identifies generative-system risks. OWASP and MITRE ATLAS organize concrete adversarial behaviors. Statistical guidance on binomial intervals prevents false certainty from small samples. Agent evaluation research contributes task environments, but security requires consequence-grounded oracles and authority-aware scenario coverage. The synthesis is a repeated, paired, isolated experiment with confidence bounds and explicit utility loss.

Sources and Further Reading

  • NIST AI RMF 1.0: https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/NIST.AI.100-1.pdf
  • NIST AI 600-1, Generative AI Profile: https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/NIST.AI.600-1.pdf
  • OWASP GenAI Security Project: https://genai.owasp.org/
  • MITRE ATLAS: https://atlas.mitre.org/
  • NIST/SEMATECH, binomial confidence intervals: https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/prc/section2/prc241.htm
  • Wilson, Probable Inference, the Law of Succession, and Statistical Inference: https://www.jstor.org/stable/2248530
  • UK AI Security Institute, Inspect AI: https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/
  • METR, agent evaluation resources: https://metr.org/

Interview Practicum

A vendor claims its new tool-call firewall cut prompt-injection success from 20 percent to zero in ten trials. Your coding agent serves 50,000 monthly tasks. You have two weeks and a constrained evaluation budget. After you propose a test, the vendor reveals that its control increases refusals and that the production model changes without notice.

Design the evaluation, quantify what the current evidence means, define release gates, and explain how you will handle adaptive attacks and model drift.

Worked Answer

Zero successes in ten does not establish zero risk; the approximate 95 percent upper bound is 30 percent. I would build a versioned suite from the Chapter 34 authority graph: indirect injection, delegation, credential access, egress, memory poisoning, tool confusion, and approval binding, plus benign tasks that exercise the same tools. Critical paths receive more trials than low-impact families.

Run baseline and firewall configurations paired on identical scenario instances, randomized in order, in isolated sandboxes. Record model/provider identity, scaffold, tool, policy, and seed where available. Automatic oracles inspect forbidden state transitions; blinded reviewers handle semantic ambiguity. Report ASR and Wilson intervals per family, benign task success, false refusal, latency, cost, and human escalation.

The release gate includes zero critical must-pass outcomes, bounded upper ASR per high-risk family, and a predeclared non-inferiority margin for task success and false refusal. A small adaptive team gets a fixed attempt budget after the static suite, while a private holdout remains untouched. Because the model changes without notice, provider identity becomes a blocking observability requirement or contractual risk; run daily sentinels and trigger the full suite on detected change. Canary deployment uses reduced authority and an immediate rollback path.

Follow-Up Questions and Answers

How many trials are enough?

Enough is claim-dependent. With zero failures, about 300 representative independent trials support an approximate 95 percent upper bound below 1 percent. Clustered or heterogeneous trials require more careful design, not merely more repetitions.

The control blocks attacks by blocking all tool calls. Did it pass?

No. Its ASR may be low, but task success and false refusal expose that it eliminated the product’s function. Security and utility are joint constraints.

Should adaptive results enter the same ASR as static tests?

Report them separately. Adaptive trials have conditional, budget-dependent sampling. Combining them with fixed random trials produces a number with unclear meaning.

What if human reviewers disagree?

Use a written rubric, blinded independent ratings, agreement statistics, and adjudication. Preserve both original judgments. Frequent disagreement means the oracle or scenario contract is underspecified.

Key Takeaways

  • Evaluate distributions of outcomes across repeated trials, not memorable transcripts.
  • Pair security metrics with benign utility, refusal, latency, cost, and escalation.
  • Report confidence intervals per threat family and protect catastrophic must-pass cases.
  • Isolate trials and ground oracles in tool-side state and typed traces.
  • Separate fixed regression, mutation, and adaptive attack evidence.
  • Re-run evaluations whenever models, scaffolds, tools, or policies change.

Field lesson: benchmark contracts must fail closed

The sec-pr project registered 564 benchmark contracts, while the single recorded benchmark run returned insufficient_evidence. Registration did not become an invented pass count. The harness exercised its fail-closed status path and preserved the difference between executable evaluation structure and mature human outcome evidence. The full case appears in Chapter 47.

Chapter 37: AI-Powered Detection and Security Operations

An SOC agent should be judged by the evidence it preserves, the consequential actions it refuses to take, and the facts it notices or misses—not by how fluent its incident summary sounds. This chapter builds such an agent for a concrete workflow: enrich an identity alert, assemble a cited case brief, identify missing evidence, recommend a disposition, and request approval for containment. The agent may read narrowly scoped systems and draft work; it may not silently expand its investigation, change a control, disable an account, or convert uncertainty into fact.

The design separates three questions that are often collapsed. Did the agent retrieve the right evidence? Did it reason faithfully over that evidence? Was it authorized to perform the requested action? Better prompting cannot repair a missing audit source, and a well-grounded conclusion does not grant authority. Production safety depends on keeping those questions separate in data, policy, evaluation, and incident review.

The Case: Impossible Travel with a Plausible Explanation

An identity provider raises an impossible-travel alert for alice@example.com: Chicago at 14:02 UTC and Amsterdam at 14:17 UTC. A weak assistant paraphrases the alert and recommends account suspension. A useful investigator checks whether both events represent human sessions, whether an approved egress proxy explains one location, whether device identity and token lineage agree, and whether high-value actions followed. It then distinguishes observation, inference, and unknown.

The desired output is not merely “benign” or “malicious.” It is a compact evidence packet: a timeline whose factual claims cite immutable evidence identifiers; explicit coverage of required questions; an omission list for unavailable or unexamined evidence; a calibrated disposition; proposed actions checked against policy; and the model, prompt, retriever, policy, and tool versions needed for replay. This packet makes the agent a participant in an evidence process rather than an oracle.

Bounded Authority Is a Capability System

“Human in the loop” is too vague to be a control. The useful unit is a capability: a narrowly defined operation over a resource class, subject to conditions, expiry, and an approval mode. Reading the last 24 hours of sign-in metadata is different from reading mailbox contents. Adding a case note is different from disabling a principal. A capability token should be minted for the case, not inherited from the service account’s broad permissions.

flowchart LR
    A[Alert envelope] --> P[Case planner]
    P --> G{Capability gateway}
    G -->|read:idp.signins| I[Identity telemetry]
    G -->|read:asset.posture| E[Endpoint posture]
    G -->|read:change.approvals| C[Change records]
    I --> V[Evidence vault]
    E --> V
    C --> V
    V --> S[Cited case synthesis]
    S --> O[Omission and contradiction check]
    O --> D{Disposition policy}
    D -->|draft only| N[Case note]
    D -->|approval required| H[Analyst approval]
    H -->|signed approval| R[Response broker]
    R --> L[Append-only action ledger]
    G --> L
    S --> L

The gateway accepts typed requests, not arbitrary URLs or shell strings. The response broker independently rechecks authorization; it does not trust a claim that approval exists. High-impact actions use a short-lived, single-use approval bound to the exact subject and action. An approval for revoke_sessions/alice cannot authorize disable_user/alice, and neither can be replayed against Bob.

OperationDefaultRequired control
Read alert-linked sign-ins, 24 hallowcase-scoped token; field minimization
Read endpoint posture for linked deviceallowasset relation must be evidenced
Search unrelated identitiesdenyanalyst expands scope with reason
Draft timeline and case noteallowcitations and model provenance
Publish note to caseallowschema validation; no action side effect
Revoke active sessionsapprovalnamed analyst; exact target; 10-minute expiry
Disable identity or isolate hostdenyincident commander or separate policy
Modify detection or suppression ruledenychange-management workflow only

The model never possesses ambient response credentials. It proposes an intent. Deterministic infrastructure decides whether that intent is permitted.

Evidence Objects, Claims, and Provenance

Retrieval grounding becomes auditable only when evidence has stable identity and claims have machine-checkable citations. A minimal contract is:

{
  "$id": "soc-evidence-v1",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["evidence_id", "observed_at", "source", "subject", "payload_hash"],
  "properties": {
    "evidence_id": {"type": "string", "pattern": "^ev_[a-f0-9]{12}$"},
    "observed_at": {"type": "string", "format": "date-time"},
    "source": {"enum": ["idp", "edr", "proxy", "cmdb", "change"]},
    "subject": {"type": "string"},
    "event_type": {"type": "string"},
    "payload_hash": {"type": "string", "pattern": "^sha256:"},
    "fields": {"type": "object"},
    "retrieved_at": {"type": "string", "format": "date-time"},
    "retention_class": {"enum": ["case", "restricted", "ephemeral"]}
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}

The narrative is stored as claims, not one unconstrained blob:

{
  "claim_id": "cl_07",
  "text": "The Amsterdam address was an approved corporate egress node.",
  "claim_type": "observation",
  "citations": ["ev_9c14d8f0a612", "ev_a82f38de7710"],
  "confidence": 0.98,
  "contradicts": []
}

claim_type may be observation, inference, or unknown. Observations must be directly entailed by cited fields. Inferences require citations and a stated inference rule. Unknowns cite the failed query or unavailable source when possible. The payload hash detects mutation; the retrieval timestamp shows what the agent could have known at decision time.

Retrieval needs defenses. Alert text is untrusted data and may contain instruction-like content. The planner extracts typed entities, but no retrieved string becomes a system instruction. Connectors impose row limits and time windows. Results are normalized and rendered as data. The planner cannot ask a connector to “run whatever query is in this event.”

Citation Quality Is More Than Citation Presence

An answer can cite every sentence and still be wrong. Evaluation therefore works at claim level. For generated claims \(C\), let \(s(c)=1\) when cited evidence supports claim \(c\), \(a(c)=1\) when it requires a citation, and \(w_c\) represent consequence weight:

\[ P_{cite}=\frac{\sum_{c\in C}w_c s(c)}{\sum_{c\in C}w_c a(c)}. \]

Citation completeness measures whether citation-requiring claims have a reference. Entailment is separate: a sign-in record supports “a login occurred,” but not “Alice performed the login.” Temporal validity matters too; evidence observed after containment cannot justify the earlier decision.

Automated checks can reject nonexistent evidence IDs, wrong subjects, evidence outside the case horizon, and claims whose cited fields lack referenced values. Human adjudication remains necessary for semantic entailment. Sample more heavily for containment recommendations, contradictions, new model versions, and low-confidence cases.

Omission Is a First-Class Error

Hallucinations are visible. Omissions often are not. An investigation that correctly describes two logins but fails to check token reuse may be more dangerous than one awkward sentence. Each alert family therefore has a question set \(Q\): device continuity, network explanation, authentication strength, token lineage, privileged follow-on activity, endpoint state, and relevant change records for impossible travel.

For question \(q\), assign importance \(v_q\) and coverage state answered, unavailable, not_applicable, or unexamined. Weighted omission loss is

\[ L_{omit}=\frac{\sum_{q\in Q}v_q\mathbb{1}[q=\text{unexamined}] +\lambda\sum_{q\in Q}v_q\mathbb{1}[q=\text{unavailable}]} {\sum_{q\in Q}v_q},\quad 0\leq\lambda<1. \]

Unavailable evidence is not equivalent to negligence, but it still weakens the decision. not_applicable requires a reason. Connector health and query logs prevent the agent from obtaining a good score by labeling every hard question unavailable.

Coverage sets should come from incident retrospectives and analyst playbooks, then remain small enough to discriminate. They are not rigid scripts. Novel evidence may add questions, while policy defines the minimum set before a close recommendation.

Decision, Abstention, and Adversarial Failure

Let \(d\) be a disposition, \(x\) the evidence, and \(L(d,y)\) the loss if the true state is \(y\):

\[ d^*=\arg\min_d\sum_yP(y\mid x)L(d,y), \quad\text{subject to }L_{omit}\leq\tau_o\text{ and }P_{cite}\geq\tau_c. \]

If constraints fail, the correct output is abstention with a specific request: “EDR posture unavailable for device D17; analyst review required.” Confidence is never authorization. A 0.99 malicious probability can justify urgency, not bypass approval.

Threat modeling must include prompt injection in alert fields, poisoned knowledge articles, cross-tenant retrieval, stale identity mappings, citation laundering, compromised connectors, approval replay, tool argument substitution, denial-of-wallet, and analyst automation bias. The strongest boundary is typed mediation: retrieved text cannot alter policy; generated text cannot become a tool call; a validated intent cannot become an action without a fresh capability check.

Safe Lab: Score a Cited Investigation

This standard-library program evaluates evidence identity, claim support, question coverage, and allowed actions. It contacts no systems and performs no containment.

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import FrozenSet

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Evidence:
    eid: str
    facts: FrozenSet[str]

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Claim:
    text: str
    required_facts: FrozenSet[str]
    citations: tuple[str, ...]
    weight: int

evidence = {
    "ev_idp": Evidence("ev_idp", frozenset({"user:alice", "mfa:pass", "device:D17"})),
    "ev_proxy": Evidence("ev_proxy", frozenset({"ip:203.0.113.8", "approved_egress:true"})),
    "ev_edr": Evidence("ev_edr", frozenset({"device:D17", "health:normal"})),
}
claims = [
    Claim("MFA succeeded on D17", frozenset({"mfa:pass", "device:D17"}), ("ev_idp",), 2),
    Claim("The foreign IP is approved egress", frozenset({"approved_egress:true"}), ("ev_proxy",), 3),
    Claim("No endpoint alerts exist", frozenset({"alerts:none"}), ("ev_edr",), 3),
]
questions = {
    "device_continuity": (3, "answered"),
    "network_explanation": (3, "answered"),
    "token_lineage": (4, "unavailable"),
    "endpoint_state": (2, "answered"),
    "privileged_follow_on": (5, "unexamined"),
}
allowed = {"read_case", "draft_note"}
proposed = ["draft_note", "revoke_sessions"]

def supported(claim: Claim) -> bool:
    cited = [evidence[e] for e in claim.citations if e in evidence]
    union = frozenset().union(*(item.facts for item in cited))
    return claim.required_facts <= union

supported_weight = sum(c.weight for c in claims if supported(c))
total_weight = sum(c.weight for c in claims)
denom = sum(weight for weight, _ in questions.values())
loss = sum(weight * (1 if state == "unexamined" else 0.35 if state == "unavailable" else 0)
           for weight, state in questions.values()) / denom
blocked = [action for action in proposed if action not in allowed]

print(f"citation_precision={supported_weight / total_weight:.3f}")
print(f"omission_loss={loss:.3f}")
print(f"unsupported={[c.text for c in claims if not supported(c)]}")
print(f"blocked_actions={blocked}")
print("decision=ABSTAIN" if loss > 0.20 else "decision=RECOMMEND")

Expected output:

citation_precision=0.625
omission_loss=0.376
unsupported=['No endpoint alerts exist']
blocked_actions=['revoke_sessions']
decision=ABSTAIN

The negative claim is unsupported: health:normal does not establish that no alerts exist. The omission score exposes unchecked privileged activity. Policy blocks response even though drafting is allowed.

Production Operations

Deploy in modes, beginning with replay on closed cases and then shadowing live investigations. In assist mode, place the draft in a separate pane. Only after demonstrated citation precision, omission control, and analyst acceptance should it publish schema-valid notes. Response authority is a distinct promotion with its own hazard review.

Operational telemetry includes connector success by source, evidence age, retrieval truncation, invalid citations, weighted omission, contradiction rate, abstention reason, analyst edits, approval latency, denied tool calls, and downstream reversals. “Minutes saved” belongs beside investigation quality. Measure time to a correct, reviewable decision; otherwise the system can look efficient by producing fast rework.

Treat analyst edits as structured feedback, not automatically correct labels. Record whether an analyst changed a fact, inference, disposition, omission state, or prose. Outcome labels arrive late and selectively. Preserve a random audit sample of closed and escalated cases to limit policy-induced label bias.

Run drills for connector outage, stale asset inventory, poisoned alert text, approval-service failure, evidence-vault unavailability, model timeout, and ledger mismatch. Fail closed for actions. For synthesis, degrade to a visible partial-evidence state. A kill switch should disable tool execution without disabling access to preserved case evidence.

  • NIST, SP 800-61 Rev. 2: Computer Security Incident Handling Guide, 2012: https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.800-61r2
